item.title: World News Brief: Nov 11, PM
item.description:
Top line

Tonight's lead: Iran is widening its threats. Its top security official says any US base used in a new war, including bases in Europe, would be a target. Reuters sources say Iran attacked shipping navigation equipment on Oman's Didamar Island. In Ukraine, the Abu Dhabi talks ended with a "large-scale" prisoner exchange agreed but no breakthrough. Within hours, Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv. In US politics, Democrat Scott Colom upset Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Threats to bases in Europe. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on X that if the US launches another war, every military base involved would be a target, including ones in Europe (Iran International, 6:27 PM ET). Commentators on state TV called for fully closing the Strait of Hormuz to force US concessions (Iran International, 6:02 PM ET). Deputy chief of staff Keyoumars Heydari said the armed forces have an updated list of possible targets "in the region and beyond" (Iran International, 2:50 PM ET). An analyst told Al Jazeera that Tehran may be deliberately pushing its retaliation beyond the Middle East (Al Jazeera, 2:14 PM ET).
  • Hormuz and Oman. Sources told Reuters that Iran attacked shipping navigation systems on Oman's Didamar Island (Reuters, 2:10 PM ET). Reuters-verified footage shows a tanker burning near Oman, with oil spills reaching Oman's shores (Iran International, 6:15 PM ET). According to an X story summary, US Central Command says its blockade has turned back 150 vessels and blocked about $30 billion in Iranian oil exports. That figure hasn't been checked against a major outlet (X story summary). Saudi Arabia has raised crude output to its highest level since the war began in February (Al Jazeera, 4:16 PM ET; Reuters, 3:45 PM ET).
  • Washington. At a Veterans Day event at Arlington, President Trump said it was time for the US to secure a "complete victory" over Iran (Al Jazeera, 2:41 PM ET). Citing two officials, The Wall Street Journal reports that Trump has privately questioned whether the Pakistan-brokered June agreement with Iran was a costly mistake that let Tehran regroup (Iran International citing WSJ, 4:50 PM ET).
  • Israel. Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot wrote to caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu warning him against dangerous military moves that could wait for a new government. Reports say Netanyahu and military chiefs disagree on possible action (Iran International, 4:56 PM ET). Contradicting Trump, Netanyahu's office says Israel will move off US military aid only "gradually" (Times of Israel, 11:22 AM ET).
  • Diplomacy and the UN. The UN General Assembly elected Iran to its Committee for Programme and Coordination with 144 votes (Iran International, 2:21 PM ET). Canada says it voted no (Iran International, 5:29 PM ET). At the COP31 summit in Turkey, President Pezeshkian said US-Israeli strikes released 1.5 million tonnes of CO2, and Iran is seeking compensation for environmental damage (Al Jazeera, 4:40 PM ET; Reuters, 5:20 PM ET).
  • Inside Iran. Videos show students at Islamic Azad University's Central Tehran branch taking off their hijabs as they leave campus, defying the mandatory hijab rules (Iran International, 5:56 PM ET). Iran is adding 23 commemorations to its official calendar, including days for the war and the killing of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei (Iran International, 3:42 PM ET). Rights activists are drawing attention to death sentences against several men arrested in January's protests. This comes from an X story summary of activists' posts (X story summary).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Kyiv under attack. Breaking: Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv hours after the peace talks ended. Kyiv Independent journalists reported several explosions around 1 AM local time, which was about 6 PM ET (Kyiv Independent, 6:37 PM ET). There are no damage or casualty reports yet.
  • Talks end. The second day in Abu Dhabi ended with a "large-scale" prisoner exchange agreed, according to Ukraine's Rustem Umerov. Russia's Vladimir Medinsky confirmed it (Kyiv Independent, 9:58 AM ET). The BBC says the talks turned to post-war security but ended without a breakthrough (BBC, 10:08 AM ET). Medinsky said there was some progress but no role for the EU for now (Reuters, 4:00 PM ET). He also repeated Russia's rejection of Ukraine's territorial integrity (Kyiv Independent, 10:32 AM ET). Zelensky is in Dublin for the European Political Community summit and expects to be briefed by US envoys Witkoff and Kushner (Kyiv Independent, 1:43 PM ET).
  • Strikes. Russia hit six major power substations in Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Zhytomyr and Cherkasy regions, causing outages across Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 11:26 AM ET). Hackers took over the website of Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform (Kyiv Independent, 2:35 PM ET). Drones hit Gazprom's Omsk refinery in Siberia, Russia's largest, about 2,500 km from Ukraine, in an eight-hour attack (Kyiv Independent, 5:57 PM ET). ISW says neither side advanced on Nov. 10 (ISW, 11:00 AM ET).
  • Iran link. Zelensky warned that the chance of new US strikes on Iran, and air-defense missiles going to the Middle East, are weakening Ukraine's ability to defend itself (Iran International, 5:16 PM ET).
  • Other. Russia's foreign ministry says Russia's ambassador to the US has died (Reuters, 6:10 PM ET). Ukraine captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war as Russia recruits more foreigners (Kyiv Independent, 2:17 PM ET). Ireland and Ukraine are considering producing drones together (BBC, 6:30 PM ET). US companies are avoiding Russian diesel, and a tanker carrying it is idling off the East Coast (Reuters, 3:40 PM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Gaza. Breaking: Gaza's Civil Defence says an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis killed at least four Palestinians (Al Jazeera, 6:38 PM ET). In Deir el-Balah, a sand embankment collapsed in heavy rain and killed three children and a woman (Reuters, 10:00 AM ET). Al Jazeera puts Wednesday's death toll from Israeli attacks at eight or more (Al Jazeera, 2:01 PM ET).
  • Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Saudi air defenses intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles fired at Riyadh (Reuters, 10:20 AM ET). The Houthis say they hit an oil pumping station in Yanbu with a drone. That is their own claim (Iran International, 1:58 PM ET). The WHO counts 2,098 killed and 9,657 wounded in Yemen's fighting as of Nov. 8 (Al Jazeera, 1:42 PM ET).
  • Lebanon. Lebanon's army chief met German defense officials to plan for after the UN peacekeeping mission (UNIFIL) ends on Dec. 31 (Al Jazeera, 2:13 PM ET).
  • US–China. China's foreign minister called his phone call with Secretary of State Rubio "positive and constructive" (Reuters, 6:40 PM ET).

Other world news

  • US politics. Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi. He becomes the state's first Black US senator since 1881 (AP, 6:06 PM ET; Reuters, 6:11 PM ET). At the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sentinel rebuked Defense Secretary Hegseth's group after laughter was heard (AP, 5:50 PM ET).
  • Business. The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang (Reuters citing WSJ, 6:30 PM ET). Markets are pricing in a hawkish Fed (Reuters, 3:50 PM ET).
  • Europe. Millions of Spaniards held the country's first general strike in 14 years, over housing (Reuters, 3:42 PM ET). An advisory panel warned Germany to rein in its military borrowing (AFP, 3:47 PM ET).
  • Africa. Leaders of Uganda's ruling party are pushing back on President Museveni's plan to make his son his successor (AFP, 6:30 PM ET).
  • Church. Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru, his "second homeland," for the first time since his election (AP, 5:12 PM ET).
  • New York. Emergency crews are searching debris after a building collapsed in Brooklyn (Reuters, 6:19 PM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 11, AM
item.description:
Top line

The biggest overnight news is from Abu Dhabi. Officials at the US-mediated talks say Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large prisoner-of-war release as the second day of talks got underway. On Iran, Tehran is hardening its line. Its top security official says none of Iran's enriched uranium will leave the country and that Iran is waiting for a US answer to its seven conditions. Another tanker caught fire after hitting a mine near Hormuz, which pushed oil prices back up.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Nuclear red line. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told Al Mayadeen that Iran won't move any enriched nuclear material abroad, will use it itself, and has told Russia this (Iran International, 4:24 AM ET). He said Tehran is waiting for a US response to its seven conditions for peace talks and brushed off talk of negotiations with Washington (Al Jazeera, 4:53 AM ET).
  • Hormuz. Iran's navy says a tanker caught fire after hitting a sea mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, in an area it calls "unsafe and restricted." This comes from Iranian state media (Al Jazeera, 2:21 AM ET; Iran International, 1:56 AM ET). Oil rebounded as the shipping attacks cut into hopes for a truce (Reuters, 3:30 AM ET). Smoke was seen rising from Oman's Didamar Island after Tuesday's attack on navigation equipment, which Iranian state media blamed on the Revolutionary Guards' navy (Iran International, 4:28 AM ET).
  • Threats. Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, said any country that helps enforce a "hostile blockade" on Iran would be treated as taking part in an act of war (Iran International, 6:22 AM ET). Armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi warned the US and Israel of more lethal strikes on any "center of threats" (Iran International, 3:18 AM ET). The hardline newspaper Kayhan urged threats against US bases beyond the region, including in Europe (Iran International, 1:46 AM ET). Iraq's Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba militia pledged loyalty to Khamenei and said it's ready for escalation, according to Kurdish media (Al Jazeera, 2:45 AM ET).
  • Military displays. Iran showed off an underground "missile city" run by the Revolutionary Guards' aerospace force. Details come from an X story summary of the unveiling, not from a major outlet (X story summary). Tehran's Guards commander said Iran kept making missiles and drones during the 40-day war and has "surprises" ready (Iran International, 4:58 AM ET). Iran also opened its first all-women military training camp (Al Jazeera, 11:00 PM ET Tue).
  • Diplomacy. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi asked the UN and the IAEA to condemn a US offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program. Iran says the offer encourages the killing of its scientists (Iran International, 2:51 AM ET; Al Jazeera, 5:06 AM ET). Iran designated Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations" to retaliate for Argentina's blacklisting of the Revolutionary Guards (Reuters, 5:30 AM ET). Activists are pushing for a recorded vote today at the UN General Assembly on Iran's nomination to a UN program-review committee (X story summary).
  • US threats and politics. The US embassy in Riyadh told Americans across the Middle East to be extra vigilant, citing threats from the Houthis and alleged Iranian efforts to target US officials (Al Jazeera, 11:46 PM ET Tue). US media report that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life. This hasn't been independently confirmed (Al Jazeera citing US media, 9:59 PM ET Tue). Sen. Adam Schiff says Democrats will use upcoming government funding talks to try to cut off money for the war (Al Jazeera, 10:34 PM ET Tue). Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican, brought the failed Hegseth impeachment bid and was the only member of his party to oppose killing it (AFP, 8:44 PM ET Tue).
  • Inside Iran. The labor news agency ILNA reports that workers buried in debt are advertising their kidneys and other organs for sale (Iran International, 6:30 AM ET). Students are reportedly in unheated classrooms as the government warns of gas shortages (Iran International, 5:29 AM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Prisoner deal. Breaking: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large release of prisoners of war, according to officials at the Abu Dhabi talks (AP, 6:59 AM ET). No numbers yet.
  • Talks, day two. The second day of the three-way talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US has begun, and Ukraine plans a separate meeting with European partners afterward (Kyiv Independent, 5:11 AM ET). Washington called for a "new" security framework on day one (AFP, 8:00 PM ET Tue). Zelenskyy said he's very happy with the messages he's getting from the US (Reuters, 12:36 AM ET). ISW says the Kremlin is trying to steer the talks toward reshaping European security, which would revive its 2021 demands to roll back NATO (ISW, 11:09 PM ET Tue).
  • Strikes on Russia. Ukrainian drones reportedly hit the Ust-Luga Baltic oil port in Leningrad region overnight (Kyiv Independent, 8:07 PM ET Tue). According to an X story summary, the local governor confirmed a fire and three injured workers (X story summary). Reuters industry sources say Ukraine's strikes since late October have cut Russia's refining capacity by about 30%. That figure comes via an X summary (X story summary).
  • Strikes on Ukraine. Russian drones hit power substations in Kryvyi Rih and caused widespread outages, according to an X story summary of local officials' posts (X story summary). Unconfirmed: Russia's defense ministry claimed it shot down four US-made AGM-188A "Rusty Dagger" cruise missiles, then removed the claim. Ukraine hasn't commented (X story summary).
  • Baltics and spying. Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia withdrew a flurry of shelter alerts over unidentified drones from Russia or Belarus (Reuters, 1:55 AM ET). Russia says it arrested two suspected Polish spies in Kaliningrad (Reuters citing Interfax, 1:50 AM ET). ISW says Iran and Russia are working together to get around US efforts to stop arms shipments over the Caspian Sea (ISW, 8:12 PM ET Tue).
  • Europe. EU Council President Costa is keeping Ukraine funding on the late-November agenda despite an appeal from Germany's Merz (Kyiv Independent, 10:25 PM ET Tue). Reuters reports that Ukraine's path to EU membership is narrowing as the war drags on (Reuters, 6:45 AM ET). Today is also four years since Kherson was liberated (X story summary).
  • Africa. US Africa Command warned Madagascar about its growing military ties with Russia (BBC, 2:34 AM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Gaza. An Israeli airstrike on a metal foundry in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood killed three people, and four more, including a 13-year-old, were killed elsewhere, medics said (Reuters, 3:34 AM ET). Gaza's health ministry says at least eight were killed in the past 24 hours (Al Jazeera, 6:05 AM ET). Sen. Brian Schatz urged Israel to let in building and winter supplies after flooding hit more than 70,000 tents and killed four people, three of them children (Al Jazeera, 1:15 AM ET).
  • Yemen. Heavy fighting goes on. Government-aligned forces claim they killed or wounded at least 190 Houthi fighters (Al Jazeera, 1:45 AM ET).
  • Taiwan. Some US federal employees will work in Taiwan government offices for up to a year under a new program (Reuters, 2:00 AM ET). Taipei named Acer's founder as its APEC envoy and called for written guarantees from China (Reuters, 4:00 AM ET).
  • Congo. Confirmed Ebola cases have passed 11,000, with at least 5,387 deaths, according to government data (Al Jazeera, 12:56 AM ET).

Other world news

  • Italy. At least 300 schools were evacuated after receiving the same bomb threat (Reuters, 6:11 AM ET).
  • Climate. Brazil's Lula told the COP31 summit that climate change has "disappeared" from the global agenda (AFP, 5:58 AM ET). In Chile, transport workers blocked highways over surging fuel prices (BBC, 6:37 AM ET).
  • Economy. A hotter-than-expected US inflation report has revived fears of a bigger Fed rate hike next month (Reuters, 6:00 AM ET). Anthropic began its IPO roadshow at a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion (Reuters, 6:10 AM ET).
  • China tech. Reuters reports that a university linked to China's military bought Nvidia's H200 AI chips despite being on a US export blacklist (Reuters, 6:45 AM ET).
  • Venezuela. Lawmakers opened the struggling power sector to private investment (AFP, 10:16 PM ET Tue).
  • Ireland. Pro-Palestinian protesters threw milk at former President Joe Biden during a visit to Trinity College Dublin (Al Jazeera, 11:40 PM ET Tue).
  • Argentina. Pope Leo wrapped up his visit (Reuters, 5:45 AM ET).

Other world news

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 10, AM
item.description:
Top line

Trump says he's holding off on new strikes against Iran after appeals from Gulf states, and the BBC quotes him calling the war "effectively over" militarily. Tehran isn't echoing that: Foreign Minister Araghchi says there are no plans for a Rezaei–Vance meeting, the Revolutionary Guards say Hormuz won't go back to its prewar status and claim two tankers caught fire in the strait, and state TV showed off a new underground missile site. Qatar's prime minister flew straight from Washington to the G7 in Paris to brief Europeans and the Saudis. The US also pulled aircraft out of a second British base over an Iranian threat, and France summoned Iran's ambassador over the supermarket fridge hack. In Ukraine, the first US–Russia–Ukraine talks in nine months opened in Abu Dhabi, while Russian attacks killed 9 people over the past day. Oil is at its lowest since August. Covers roughly 7 PM Monday to 7 AM ET Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Trump holds fire. Trump said he plans to hold off on new military strikes for now after appeals from regional countries, including Qatar's prime minister (Reuters, 9:15 PM ET), and the BBC reports he called the war "effectively over" militarily with further strikes unlikely (BBC, 9:39 PM ET).
  • Tehran's line. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said there are no plans for security chief Mohsen Rezaei to meet Vice President Vance, contradicting Turkey's intelligence chief, and said the war won't end through military action or more sanctions (Iran International, 2:44 AM ET). First Vice President Mohammadreza Aref said "confrontation with the enemy will continue" whether or not peace is reached (Iran International, 6:46 AM ET), and one lawmaker called for Iran to build and stockpile nuclear weapons (Iran International, 6:00 AM ET). ISW assesses that Rezaei's growing role in the talks means Iran will likely stick to maximalist demands, including recognized control of Hormuz (ISW, 9:40 PM ET).
  • Mediation. Qatar's prime minister made an unscheduled stop at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris to brief European powers and Saudi Arabia after his Trump talks (Reuters, 4:10 AM ET; Iran International, 5:48 AM ET). Qatar's foreign ministry says it has received positive responses from both Washington and Tehran (Iran International citing Al Jazeera, 6:34 AM ET). Russia's ambassador says Moscow's offer to take about 400 kg of Iran's highly enriched uranium still stands (Iran International, 3:49 AM ET). Unconfirmed: an X news summary describes a Qatari–Pakistani framework allowing 3.67% enrichment, IAEA inspections and unfreezing $6–9 billion in exchange for lifting the blockade; US officials haven't confirmed any terms (X news summary).
  • Hormuz. The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers caught fire in the strait, including a supertanker it says hit a naval mine; that's the Guards' claim and not independently confirmed in the posts reviewed (Iran International, 5:50 AM ET). The IRGC's Tehran commander said the strait won't return to its prewar status and Iran will keep controlling shipping (Iran International, 1:58 AM ET). State media also aired senior commanders touring a new underground missile facility, without saying where it is or when the visit happened (Iran International, 6:49 AM ET).
  • Threats abroad. The US moved tankers and tiltrotor aircraft out of RAF Mildenhall in England over an Iranian threat, the second British base thinned out since a suspected Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford in September (Reuters citing WSJ, 2:00 AM ET; Iran International, 5:08 AM ET). France summoned Iran's ambassador over cyberattacks it blames on the IRGC that overheated fridges and freezers in about 700 supermarkets, and its foreign minister says it "rules nothing out" in response (Reuters, 5:00 AM ET; AFP, 3:51 AM ET; Iran International, 5:30 AM ET). Israel's foreign ministry cited both as proof Iran remains a threat beyond the Middle East (Iran International, 3:39 AM ET).
  • Sanctions and Gulf defense. Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities, including the national oil and tanker companies and four major banks, that it had delisted under the 2015 nuclear deal (Reuters, 6:20 AM ET). Gulf Cooperation Council states approved a forward headquarters for their unified military command in Kuwait (Iran International citing Al Ekhbariya, 6:01 AM ET).
  • Inside Iran. The government warns of a winter gas shortfall of up to 430 million cubic meters that could mean cuts even in Tehran (Iran International, 2:57 AM ET), and the judiciary says several people were arrested for encouraging women to defy hijab rules on Tehran's Iranshahr street (Iran International, 5:55 AM ET).
  • US politics and markets. A Reuters/Ipsos poll finds most Americans, including about half of Republicans, want Congress to pass legislation ending the war (Reuters, 12:45 AM ET), and Trump's approval holds at 32% (Reuters, 4:50 AM ET). Hegseth is due to hold a rare news conference today as he fights Rep. Massie's impeachment push (AFP, 4:52 AM ET). Oil has fallen to its lowest level since August (Reuters, 6:00 AM ET) and Gulf stock markets opened higher (Reuters, 5:45 AM ET). Reuters also has a feature on vessels and sailors who have vanished at sea during the war (Reuters, 5:10 AM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Abu Dhabi talks open. US-mediated three-way talks resumed after a nine-month pause, with Ukraine's delegation head Rustem Umerov saying the agenda covers ending hostilities (Kyiv Independent, 4:00 AM ET; AP, 4:29 AM ET). AFP says Washington is calling for a "new" security framework while Europe worries Trump wants a deal with Moscow over the continent's future (AFP, 5:18 AM ET). Ukraine met European and US officials beforehand (Kyiv Independent, 3:18 AM ET). Rubio said Monday night that security guarantees for Ukraine must also be acceptable to Russia, which drew criticism from Ukrainians (Kyiv Independent, 10:07 PM ET). Unconfirmed: an X news summary says US negotiators floated a "cartographic fudge" letting Russia claim all of Donetsk and Luhansk on paper while Ukraine keeps cities like Kramatorsk; I didn't see a wire report on it (X news summary).
  • Zelenskyy. He said the quickest way to end the war is to stop where the lines are, declare a ceasefire, and move to diplomacy (Zelenskyy, 5:56 AM ET), and called ceding land for peace "abstract words," noting Putin talked about Donbas and then went for Kyiv (Zelenskyy, 5:51 AM ET). He's now in Denmark to meet Prime Minister Frederiksen, defense companies, King Frederik and the Nordic prime ministers (Zelenskyy, 7:01 AM ET).
  • Attacks. Russian attacks killed 9 people and injured 39, including a 1-year-old, over the past day; Russia launched one Iskander-M ballistic missile and 162 long-range drones overnight (Kyiv Independent, 5:23 AM ET). Explosions were reported near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea (Kyiv Independent, 11:10 PM ET).
  • Front line. ISW says neither side advanced on Nov. 9 and notes a prominent Russian milblogger flagging fewer Russian claims of captured settlements (ISW, 9:03 PM ET). ISW also says Russia's central bank is acknowledging mounting economic strain from the war while calling it temporary (ISW, 11:30 PM ET), and that Russia very likely can't supply Iran with the air defenses it wants (ISW, 10:40 PM ET).
  • Other. Poland arrested two Ukrainians on suspicion of espionage and sabotage for Russia (Reuters, 4:45 AM ET). Foreign Minister Sybiha says a detained Ukrainian OSCE staffer, Vadym Golda, was moved to a medical-correctional facility in Russia's Tambov region (Kyiv Independent, 12:51 AM ET). Russian investigative paper Novaya Gazeta is winding down, citing state pressure (Reuters, 4:55 AM ET).

Other conflicts

  • West Bank. Israeli forces killed a Palestinian boy, according to the health ministry (BBC, 6:26 AM ET).
  • Israel politics. Opposition leaders Eisenkot, Bennett, Golan, Liberman and Lapid issued a joint statement saying they've agreed on a joint nomination ahead of coalition talks; the post was cut off before the details (Times of Israel, 4:26 AM ET).
  • Korea. North Korea accused the UN secretary-general of siding with South Korea over border tensions (Reuters, 7:00 AM ET).

Other world news

  • Bulgaria. At least 12 people were killed and dozens hurt in a string of fog-related crashes on a motorway in eastern Bulgaria (AP, 6:21 AM ET).
  • Hungary. Authorities detained Viktor Orbán's brother in a people-smuggling investigation, the prime minister says (Reuters, 6:45 AM ET).
  • Spain and Poland. A police officer died and another was hurt in a backpack explosion in Oviedo (BBC, 4:29 AM ET). Poland says the Krakow gunman had visited websites about Norwegian mass killer Anders Breivik (Reuters, 6:30 AM ET).
  • Nvidia. Shareholders sued Jensen Huang and Nvidia, alleging they were misled about his affair with an accused Chinese spy (AFP, 6:54 AM ET), as the FBI looks at whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence (Reuters, 6:41 AM ET).
  • Economy and diplomacy. China's trade surplus passed $1 trillion (Reuters, 3:45 AM ET), and the US will skip its UN human rights review, drawing criticism (Reuters, 4:30 AM ET). US October inflation data is due today and is expected to show slower price growth (Reuters, 5:35 AM ET).
  • Culture. M. John Harrison, 81, won the Booker Prize for "The End of Everything," becoming its oldest winner (Reuters, 3:59 AM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 9, PM
item.description:
Top line

After a 45-minute Oval Office meeting with Qatar’s prime minister, Trump said there was “positive momentum” toward ending the Iran war and that military action isn’t necessary “at this point,” though he says the US is ready to strike if needed and is content to keep the naval blockade. Tehran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei called the talk of progress false and demanded the US accept Iran’s seven conditions. Turkey’s intelligence chief says JD Vance and Rezaei will meet in Qatar next week. In Washington, Republican Rep. Thomas Massie filed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth over the war. Brent crude fell nearly 7%. In Ukraine, the negotiating team is already in Abu Dhabi for talks starting Tuesday, the EU plans another €45 billion for 2027, and a drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. Covers roughly 7 AM to 7 PM ET Monday, Nov. 9.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Trump–Qatar meeting. Trump and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met for about 45 minutes around noon, focused on Iran talks (Iran International citing Axios, 1:50 PM ET). The Qatari premier also met Vice President Vance and said the meetings focused on advancing US–Iran negotiations (Iran International, 5:01 PM ET); Al Jazeera, citing a source, reported “good progress” (Iran International citing Al Jazeera, 4:18 PM ET). Axios later reported Trump told him he’s willing to give talks a chance but could reverse course if Tehran doesn’t engage seriously (Iran International citing Axios, 6:51 PM ET).
  • Trump’s remarks. Trump said there was “positive momentum” toward a deal (Iran International, 5:49 PM ET), a “good chance” of agreement with Tehran “talking very politely” (Times of Israel, 5:52 PM ET), and that military action isn’t necessary “at this point” (Reuters, 6:00 PM ET). He told Reuters Qatar and Saudi Arabia want a peaceful deal, that he’s content with the Hormuz blockade, and that the US is ready to strike if needed (Reuters, 4:30 PM ET; Iran International, 4:15 PM ET). He also claimed Iran is “militarily essentially gone” and that Iran has accepted it will never have a nuclear weapon, which Tehran publicly denies (Iran International, 4:55 PM ET; Iran International, 5:28 PM ET). On Truth Social he said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait favor keeping the blockade in place (Iran International, 4:49 PM ET).
  • Tehran’s response. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei accused Washington of spreading false reports about negotiations and demanded the US accept Iran’s seven conditions (Iran International, 5:49 PM ET). Parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Israel is dragging the US into an endless war no president could escape (Iran International, 1:10 PM ET). Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin said Vance and Rezaei are scheduled to meet in Qatar next week; that hasn’t been confirmed by Washington or Tehran in the posts reviewed (Iran International, 11:07 AM ET). China says it’s in contact about a possible Xi–Putin–Trump meeting (Iran International, 9:14 AM ET).
  • Strikes and Hormuz. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that US strikes over the past week have targeted air-defense and navigation radars, missile-launcher bases and naval mine-laying systems, including on Qeshm Island (Iran International citing Reuters, 10:20 AM ET). UKMTO classified as an attack a Saturday incident in which a tanker caught fire northwest of Khasab, Oman, and its crew evacuated (Iran International, 11:45 AM ET). The UAE city of Khor Fakkan shut a beach after detecting an oil spill (Reuters, 4:50 PM ET). An X news summary says Iran struck radar and communications gear on Oman’s Didamar Island in the strait; that is unconfirmed by the wire services reviewed here (X news summary).
  • Gulf and Yemen. Saudi state media says the East-West oil pipeline was hit in the Medina region; details on who was responsible weren’t in the report’s headline (Reuters, 5:45 PM ET). Earlier, Saudi Arabia said the danger had passed in Riyadh after an alert, a day after a Houthi attack (Reuters, 7:40 AM ET), and the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi ballistic-missile component factory and a missile-fuel plant at unspecified locations (Iran International, 1:51 PM ET).
  • France. French officials blame Iran for cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators that spoiled tens of millions of euros of food, and vow retaliation (Reuters exclusive, 3:35 PM ET). In Israel, police and Shin Bet are investigating threatening leaflets suspected to come from Iran found in north Tel Aviv mailboxes (Iran International citing Kan, 8:47 AM ET).
  • Washington politics. Rep. Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, including waging war on Iran without congressional approval, starting a two-day clock toward an expected House vote (Reuters, 6:14 PM ET; AFP, 4:00 PM ET). Hegseth played down the risk (Reuters, 6:35 PM ET) and Trump called Massie “a sick guy” (Iran International, 5:31 PM ET). House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said Iran is stronger after the campaign and vowed to end the war (Iran International, 4:52 PM ET).
  • Markets. Brent crude fell nearly 7% to $91.61 on hopes of a diplomatic resolution (Iran International, 3:37 PM ET), and the S&P 500 jumped 2.3%, its biggest gain since April (AP, 4:11 PM ET). A Reuters survey found OPEC output in October rose to 90% of its pre-war rate (Reuters, 6:40 PM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Abu Dhabi talks. Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s negotiators are already in the UAE, the first meeting is Tuesday, and European partners will join in separate formats (Zelenskyy, 4:13 PM ET). Ukraine’s negotiator said Italy will also take part, separate from the trilateral format (Kyiv Independent, 8:14 AM ET). At the G7 in Paris, European ministers pressed Secretary of State Rubio to make sure any settlement is fair to Ukraine (AFP, 11:50 AM ET). Zelenskyy also briefed India’s Modi and asked India to help push for an end to the war (Zelenskyy, 9:02 AM ET; Kyiv Independent, 10:29 AM ET). The UN Security Council met on Ukraine (Reuters, 10:29 AM ET).
  • Money and sanctions. The EU plans a new €45 billion for Kyiv in 2027 on top of its existing loan pledge (Kyiv Independent, 11:04 AM ET), and Germany’s Merz complained of unfair burden-sharing and urged the EU to prioritize a new loan (Kyiv Independent, 5:57 PM ET). An IMF mission began talks that could unlock a $1.67 billion tranche (Kyiv Independent, 8:22 AM ET), and Canada sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people tied to Russia’s missile industry and crypto exchanges (Kyiv Independent, 8:57 AM ET). The EU also activated an emergency mechanism to fund urgent energy repairs (Kyiv Independent, 8:10 AM ET).
  • Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. The IAEA says a drone strike killed a worker at the Russian-occupied plant, and a second drone killed an employee at the nearby thermal plant (Kyiv Independent, 5:00 PM ET).
  • Ukrainian strikes. Ukraine’s General Staff says it hit the Morozov plant near St. Petersburg, which it says makes ballistic-missile fuel (Kyiv Independent, 8:28 AM ET), a Russian satellite-communications jamming station (Kyiv Independent, 11:03 AM ET), and a base of Russia’s elite “Rubicon” drone unit in occupied Berdyansk (Kyiv Independent, 3:26 PM ET). These are Ukrainian military claims. Russian media report Rosneft has imposed gasoline purchase limits in Krasnoyarsk Krai amid the refinery attacks (Kyiv Independent, 7:30 AM ET).
  • Black Sea and postwar planning. Reuters reports Russia has struck cargo ships carrying military goods for Ukraine, with analysts saying it aims to cut Ukraine’s exports and test NATO red lines (Reuters podcast, 8:25 AM ET). A British- and French-led coalition began its first exercise in Poland to prepare for a postwar deployment in Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 9:50 AM ET). ISW told the FT that Russian videos claiming battlefield gains are part of a campaign to make Russian victory look inevitable (ISW citing FT, 12:09 PM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Gaza. Four people were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents, which Reuters confirms after this morning’s brief flagged it as unconfirmed (Reuters, 9:35 AM ET). The Board of Peace said Israel is holding up Hamas disarmament and must let more winter supplies into Gaza (Times of Israel, 1:07 PM ET).
  • Syria and Jordan. The two countries signed cooperation deals as they try to mend ties after deadly airstrikes (Reuters, 9:50 AM ET).

Other world news

  • Nvidia. Trump says the FBI is investigating CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman US officials say is a Chinese agent, and that Huang told him he had no idea (AP, 5:27 PM ET; BBC, 5:52 PM ET). Nvidia and Huang were sued over related disclosures (Reuters, 6:10 PM ET).
  • Poland. Tens of thousands joined a silent march in Krakow led by the president and prime minister for the victims of the weekend mass shooting (AFP, 6:30 PM ET).
  • South Africa. Analysts call the ANC’s sweeping local-election losses a vote for performance over loyalty (Reuters, 4:31 PM ET).
  • Cyprus. Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders agreed to open new border crossings and hold future talks (Reuters, 3:50 PM ET).
  • Migrants. An X news summary citing Reuters says hundreds of mostly Honduran migrants formed a caravan heading north from Tapachula, Mexico; I didn’t see the Reuters post itself (X news summary).
  • Vatican and UK. Pope Leo met Argentine clergy abuse survivors (Reuters, 6:45 PM ET), and Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assault (AP, 4:30 PM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 9, AM
item.description:
Top line

Trump meets Qatar’s prime minister, the main US–Iran mediator, at the White House today, though Reuters reports no deal to end the war looks imminent. Overnight Trump said renewed strikes were “highly unlikely” if talks progress, and Iranian officials said Sunday night’s US strike on Qeshm Island hit nothing vital. Iran says IAEA inspectors visited the Bushehr nuclear plant but insists it won’t ship enriched uranium abroad, and President Pezeshkian says the supreme leader ordered an end to the “no war, no peace” limbo. In Ukraine, Russia launched 317 drones overnight as blackouts grip Kyiv, Ukrainian drones reportedly hit a major refinery near St. Petersburg, and the Kremlin disputes that Europe will take part in this week’s Abu Dhabi talks. Covers roughly 7 PM Sunday to 7 AM ET Monday, Nov. 9.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Diplomacy via Qatar. The White House said Trump meets Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani today as Doha keeps mediating (Iran International, 7:37 PM ET Sun; Reuters, 1:10 AM ET). Reuters’ latest framing is that no imminent deal is in sight (Reuters, 6:30 AM ET). Axios reported the Qatari premier is seeking more time for diplomacy (Iran International citing Axios, 10:23 PM ET Sun). An X news summary describes a weekend proposal letting Iran enrich to 3.67% at home, down-blend about 400 kg of higher-enriched material, lift the US naval blockade and free $6–10 billion in assets; those terms are unconfirmed by the outlets cited here (X news summary).
  • Trump’s remarks. Trump repeated that new strikes were “highly unlikely” if Iran signs “a very strong agreement,” adding “I would if necessary” (AFP, 2:33 AM ET; Reuters, 9:10 PM ET Sun). He told 60 Minutes the two sides were close to a deal before the midterms and suggested Democratic wins encouraged Tehran to hold out (Iran International, 10:16 PM ET Sun), said “We won in Iran. It’s just a question of closing it out now or later” (Iran International, 8:17 PM ET Sun), and said he expects to discuss ending the war with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at next week’s APEC summit in China (Reuters, 10:45 PM ET Sun).
  • Tehran’s line. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said IAEA inspectors visited the Bushehr nuclear plant several days ago and Iran hasn’t suspended its NPT commitments (Iran International, 3:26 AM ET; Times of Israel, 5:13 AM ET). He also said Iran will not transfer enriched uranium out of the country (Iran International, 6:33 AM ET), that Iran wants measures against it lifted so it can meet its commitments within two days (Iran International, 4:35 AM ET), and that Iran sees “no difference” between US parties (Iran International, 2:53 AM ET). President Pezeshkian said the supreme leader had ordered officials to end the “no war, no peace” situation and that a dignified agreement was possible (Iran International, 5:20 AM ET). In a harder note, lawmaker Hamidreza Gudarzi argued Iran should pursue nuclear weapons as a deterrent; he is one legislator, not official policy (Iran International, 5:43 AM ET). Araghchi accused Israel of dragging successive US administrations into wars (Iran International, 11:22 PM ET Sun).
  • Qeshm strike aftermath. A Hormozgan deputy governor told state media Sunday night’s US attack on Qeshm Island hit sites outside residential and commercial areas and damaged no vital infrastructure or services (Iran International, 12:14 AM ET). The US has not publicly detailed the strike in the reporting reviewed here.
  • Hormuz. Iran said no unauthorized vessels transited the strait overnight after the IRGC Navy destroyed what it called enemy navigation aids in the southern channel; this is Iran’s own claim, not independently verified (Reuters, 3:35 AM ET). An IRGC spokesman called claims that mines had been cleared from the strait “an outright lie” (Iran International, 1:38 AM ET). Iran International, citing a confidential document, reported Iran is using terminals and storage in China to keep sanctioned tankers running (Iran International, 9:48 PM ET Sun).
  • Region and markets. UAE adviser Anwar Gargash warned of prolonged regional uncertainty and said a full US–Iran settlement looks difficult (Reuters, 2:10 AM ET). Turkey’s Erdogan said he told Trump he doesn’t want a new wave of attacks on Iran (Iran International, 5:36 AM ET). China’s Middle East envoy Zhai Jun met Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Iran (Iran International, 2:05 AM ET). Brent crude dipped to about $97.67 at the open and Gulf stocks rose on Trump’s comments (Iran International, 8:28 PM ET Sun; Reuters, 4:40 AM ET).
  • Iraq (unverified). An X news summary says Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi described to Shiite leaders a leaked US war plan involving scenarios of ground forces crossing Iraq; it rests on anonymous sources with no official confirmation (X news summary). The same feed says the PM condemned the Khor Mor gas field drone attack and opened a probe (X news summary).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Overnight attack. Russia launched 317 long-range drones, including 105 jet-powered ones, plus cruise missiles, and attacks injured 28 people across Ukraine over the past day as strikes on energy continue (Kyiv Independent, 6:55 AM ET).
  • Blackouts. Zelenskyy said he and Ursula von der Leyen agreed to activate an EU emergency mechanism for fast repair funding, with power, water and heat hardest hit in Kyiv, Dnipro, Sumy and other regions (Zelenskyy, 2:58 AM ET). AFP and the Kyiv Independent describe Kyiv residents walking darkened streets and stocking up ahead of winter (AFP, 11:46 PM ET Sun; Kyiv Independent, 5:27 AM ET). ISW says Russia is using its winter strike campaign to degrade Ukraine’s energy security (ISW, 9:00 PM ET Sun).
  • Ukrainian strikes. Ukrainian drones reportedly hit the Kirishi (Kinef) refinery, Russia’s second-largest, about 500 miles north of Ukraine, causing large explosions (Kyiv Independent, 11:07 PM ET Sun).
  • Abu Dhabi talks, Nov. 10–11. A senior EU official told the Kyiv Independent the EU, NATO and the national security advisers of Germany, France and the UK will take part (Kyiv Independent, 4:23 AM ET). Kremlin spokesman Peskov countered that the talks are trilateral between Russia and Ukraine with US mediation (Kyiv Independent, 6:41 AM ET). Trump told 60 Minutes he thinks a deal is close and that Ukraine will likely “end up with a little bit different shape” (Kyiv Independent, 9:58 PM ET Sun). G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris today (Reuters, 10:50 PM ET Sun).
  • Losses. Ukraine’s General Staff reported record Russian losses for Nov. 8 (Kyiv Independent, 5:39 AM ET); an X summary puts it at 2,980 in a day, a Ukrainian figure not independently verified (X news summary). ISW, citing analyses of data hackers say they took from Russia’s statistics agency, said Russian deaths may be near 450,000 and likely higher; Russia denies a breach (ISW, 9:45 PM ET Sun).
  • Human story. Reuters profiled an elderly couple reunited after the husband spent four and a half years trapped in Russian-held Oleshky (Reuters, 6:10 AM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Gaza (unconfirmed by wires). An X news summary reports heavy rain flooded around 70,000 tents in displacement camps, with a child reported dead from cold and five killed in an embankment collapse in Deir al-Balah; I couldn’t find this in Reuters, AP or AFP posts in this window (X news summary). A viral “Gaza snowstorm” video is being called out as AI-generated (X news summary).

Other world news

  • Senegal. The migrant boat death toll rose to 39 as more bodies were found, emergency services said (AP, 6:53 AM ET).
  • Poland. The Krakow gunman died in hospital, and prosecutors say there’s no evidence yet tying him to any ideology (Reuters, 5:54 AM ET; AFP, 6:50 AM ET).
  • Climate. COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, with an early fight over money as the UN chief urged leaders to “get serious” (AFP, 6:20 AM ET).
  • France. An EU report says a covert Russian network exploited French riots on social media (Reuters exclusive, 5:45 AM ET), as PM Lecornu holds talks on protesters’ cost-of-living concerns (Reuters, 5:50 AM ET).
  • Nvidia. CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say worked for Chinese intelligence, which Beijing denies; Nvidia shares fell as its internal probe continues (AFP, 5:50 AM ET; Reuters, 6:09 AM ET).

Overnight Trump said renewed strikes were “highly unlikely” if talks progress, and Iranian officials said Sunday night’s US strike on Qeshm Island hit nothing vital. item.description:
Top line

Explosions hit Iran’s Qeshm Island and were heard in Bandar Abbas on Sunday afternoon; the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim agency blamed a US attack, and Iranian state TV said shots near Sirik targeted “violating vessels” in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump told CNN renewed strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if talks produce a strong deal, while Secretary of State Rubio called Iran’s demands unrealistic, and Foreign Minister Araghchi warned Iran would “rain down hell” if Washington chose war. Washington asked Iraq to shut most of its border crossings with Iran, and a drone attack halted production at Iraq’s Khor Mor gas field. In Ukraine, power is being restored in the Dnipro region and Europe says it will take part in peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11. Elsewhere, South Africa’s ANC posted its worst-ever election result. Covers roughly 7 AM to 7 PM ET Sunday, Nov. 8.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Qeshm and Bandar Abbas. State news agency IRNA reported four explosions on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, with several locations apparently hit; local authorities had not yet commented (Iran International, 2:35 PM ET). The IRGC-affiliated Fars agency reported several explosions in the port city of Bandar Abbas (Iran International, 3:06 PM ET). Tasnim, also IRGC-affiliated, said a projectile fired by US forces struck Qeshm and that it was the only place hit (Iran International, 3:57 PM ET). Iranian state TV said three shots heard near Sirik were part of action against “violating vessels” in the strait (Iran International, 3:24 PM ET). There is no US confirmation of a strike in the reporting reviewed here. An X news summary describes this as a third straight night of reported US strikes on air-defense sites and says Iran fired cruise missiles from Sirik; that has not been confirmed by the outlets cited here (X news summary).
  • Trump and Rubio. Trump told CNN in a 20-minute phone interview that it was “highly unlikely” he would order renewed military action if Iran agreed to a strong deal on its nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran was eager for a deal, while warning that Washington had identified infrastructure targets (Reuters, 1:10 PM ET; Iran International, 12:49 PM ET). The Jerusalem Post, citing two sources, reported that Trump held off ordering strikes over the weekend despite US and Israeli military preparations for a possible operation (Iran International, 5:12 PM ET). Trump also said Task Force Iron Gate was operating at full strength and that, with the naval blockade, very little was moving in or out of Iran (Iran International, 4:04 PM ET). Arriving in France for a G7 foreign ministers’ meeting, Rubio said diplomacy had been unproductive because Tehran’s demands were unacceptable and unrealistic, and said a nuclear Iran “would be completely unacceptable” (Iran International, 5:36 PM ET; more, 6:38 PM ET).
  • Tehran’s line. Araghchi posted that Iran’s forces would “rain down hell” if Washington chose war instead of meeting Tehran’s demands, including an end to fighting on all fronts (Iran International, 12:16 PM ET). He later told state media that mediators had been inactive for several days because of the US election results and more time was needed before diplomacy could resume (Iran International, 2:14 PM ET). An IRGC spokesman said the US could not cut Iran off from its neighbors (Iran International, 3:44 PM ET).
  • Borders and Iraq. Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the US formally asked Iraq to close all its border crossings with Iran except two (Reuters, 6:20 PM ET). Iraq’s oil minister said Baghdad had reached understandings with the US to allow its oil exports through Hormuz (Reuters, 7:00 PM ET). An explosive-laden drone hit a gas storage facility at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan, production was suspended, and the region’s electricity ministry said nearly 2,800 megawatts of generation were lost; no one claimed the attack in the reporting reviewed here (Reuters, 4:00 PM ET; Iran International, 3:47 PM ET). Hundreds of trucks have been stuck for days at the Rimdan crossing between Iran and Pakistan, according to the rights group Haalvsh (Iran International, 2:48 PM ET).
  • Hormuz shipping. ISW said the IRGC Navy kept attacking vessels in and around the strait on Nov. 7 to pressure countries to recognize Iranian control of it, while the US kept enforcing its blockade of Iranian ports (ISW, 4:24 PM ET; more, 6:30 PM ET).
  • US politics. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries told ABC he would support impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over what he called a reckless and costly war with Iran (BBC, 2:39 PM ET; Iran International, 4:20 PM ET).
  • Inside Iran. Iran International, citing two sources, reported that 20-year-old Abolfazl Sedaghat was sentenced to death by a Revolutionary Court in Mashhad and denied a lawyer of his choosing; this is the outlet’s sourcing and not independently confirmed (Iran International, 12:20 PM ET). This follows Sunday’s executions of three Karaj protesters covered in the morning brief. Exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi said the government “has never been so brittle” (Iran International, 11:40 AM ET).
  • Israel. Supporters rallied in Tel Aviv’s Habima Square urging opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government (Reuters, 3:10 PM ET). The Times of Israel cited a report that Trump is pressing Netanyahu to advance the Gaza plan after the election (Times of Israel, 5:49 PM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Power grid. Zelenskyy said restoration work continued in the Dnipro region after strikes on Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske, and other communities, where more than 600,000 customers lost power at the peak, and he met regional heads about frontline and border regions, including Sumy (Zelenskyy, 9:27 AM ET; Zelenskyy, 10:14 AM ET). Three people, including a child, died of carbon monoxide poisoning in Kyiv Oblast after running a generator in a basement, the State Emergency Service said (Kyiv Independent, 10:21 AM ET). Zelenskyy asked the prime minister to set up free public transport in Kyiv because Russian attacks on bridges are disrupting travel (Kyiv Independent, 11:29 AM ET).
  • Kremenchuk (unconfirmed by major outlets). An X news summary reports that Russian drones hit a hotel and an apartment building in Kremenchuk Sunday evening local time, injuring at least seven people, including a 16-year-old; I couldn’t find this in Reuters, AP, AFP, or Kyiv Independent posts yet (X news summary).
  • Ukrainian strikes. The governor of Russia’s Rostov region said Ukrainian drones hit power stations and that drone debris damaged a bridge over the Mius River on a road linking Rostov to occupied Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 1:06 PM ET). ISW said Ukraine is targeting Russian missile launch sites and production plants as its air-defense stocks shrink (ISW, 10:00 AM ET). ISW also said Ukraine gained more territory than Russia in October for the second month in a row, and that Russian forces took more than 54,000 killed or seriously wounded, their highest monthly toll of the war, by its assessment (ISW, 4:00 PM ET).
  • Abu Dhabi talks. France’s foreign minister said Europe will be “well represented” at the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11, and ISW said both Kyiv and Moscow gave more details on their delegations (Kyiv Independent, 9:25 AM ET; ISW, 2:00 PM ET).
  • Sport. Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha called for a boycott and defunding of the world hockey federation after Russia was let back into the 2027 World Junior Championship in Canada, replacing Norway (Kyiv Independent, 1:57 PM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa that the Houthis had used against Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Region (Iran International, 1:28 PM ET). The BBC reported on the Aramco Tower in central Riyadh being hit as the Houthis launched fresh strikes (BBC, 4:41 PM ET). Yemen’s internationally recognized government urged Iran to stop arming the Houthis and pull out its military advisers, accusing Tehran of helping plan the group’s operations (Iran International, 5:44 PM ET).

Other world news

  • South Africa. The ANC took just over 30% in municipal elections, its worst result since the end of apartheid (AFP, 1:27 PM ET; BBC, 12:54 PM ET).
  • Senegal. At least 21 people died when a migrant boat sank off the coast, the government said; later local reports cited by an X summary put the toll at 34 or more, which is not yet confirmed (Reuters, 12:40 PM ET; X news summary).
  • Egypt. A train collision killed at least 7 and injured dozens, the health ministry said (Reuters, 2:30 PM ET).
  • Poland. A fellow shooting-club member told Reuters the Krakow gunman appeared highly skilled, and AFP reported the attack has shaken Poland’s sense of being immune to Europe’s mass shootings (Reuters, 3:10 PM ET; AFP, 3:02 PM ET).
  • Germany. Chancellor Friedrich Merz confirmed he intends to nominate Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner, who is expected to become Germany’s first woman president next year (AFP, 6:45 PM ET).
  • G7 and tech. Italy said G7 ministers will discuss recent cyber attacks (Reuters, 4:40 PM ET). Nvidia opened an investigation after a report that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence (Reuters, 3:30 PM ET).
  • Argentina. Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina and met President Javier Milei on the second leg of his South America tour (AFP, 5:17 PM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 8, AM
item.description:
Top line

Iran’s judiciary said it executed three men arrested during January protests in Karaj, the IRGC said three oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz early Sunday, and the UK’s maritime warning center separately reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile and another on fire near Oman. Israel’s defense minister said the mission against Iran’s nuclear threat is “not yet complete.” In Ukraine, Zelenskyy said Russia hit energy infrastructure overnight, leaving more than 600,000 people without power in the Dnipro region, and that an FPV drone struck a village where rescuers are still searching after a bombing that killed 55. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia damaged an Aramco building in Riyadh with falling debris; no injuries were reported. Elsewhere, Poland mourned six people killed in a Krakow shooting. Covers roughly 7 PM Saturday through 7 AM ET Sunday, Nov. 8.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Executions. Iran’s judiciary said early Sunday that it had executed Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zanganeh after the Supreme Court upheld their death sentences. The three were arrested during January protests in Karaj, west of Tehran, and had also been ordered to forfeit their assets. Authorities accused them of taking part in operations for Israel, the United States, and “hostile groups,” and of attacking public and government buildings, damaging electricity infrastructure, and disrupting services during protests on January 8 and 9. The judiciary said Divband was arrested on January 11 after a report from the Intelligence Ministry’s Alborz office and accused him of setting fire to public property; ten other people were later arrested on accusations of participating in the protests and collaborating with him. These are the judiciary’s allegations (Iran International, 11:39 PM ET Saturday).
  • Hormuz tankers. The IRGC Navy said three oil tankers caught fire early Sunday along what it called an “unauthorized route” in the Strait of Hormuz, and that smoke had spread across the waterway. It blamed the ships for switching off their navigation and identification systems and “accompanying the US military,” and warned that vessels that defy Iran’s transit rules and cooperate with the US military “will have no fate other than this.” The statement gave no names, flags, cargo details, or casualty information, and there is no independent confirmation of the cause; treat this as Iran’s account (Iran International, 5:51 AM ET). Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations center said Sunday, citing a company security officer, that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the strait on Saturday; all crew were safe and no environmental impact was reported. UKMTO also said, citing military authorities, that a tanker was on fire and its crew evacuated 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, on Saturday, near the strait. Both were delayed reports; UKMTO advised ships to transit with caution while authorities investigate. It is not clear from the reporting whether these are the same vessels described by the IRGC (projectile, 6:21 AM ET; Khasab fire, 4:25 AM ET).
  • Blockade and signaling. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi said Sunday that the US plan to restrict overland routes for weapons and sanctioned goods would fail, calling Task Force Iron Gate a plan that “will remain only on paper.” He said earlier US efforts to impose naval, air, and land blockades had also failed (Iran International, 4:17 AM ET). Armed forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi described President Trump’s political and election setbacks as evidence of a broader defeat against Iran rather than ordinary domestic politics, and said US military pressure had reached a dead end (Iran International, 2:47 AM ET). Lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi, a member of parliament’s national security committee, said US midterm results would not change Iran’s nuclear strategy and warned that any US or Israeli action would bring a severe response (Iran International, 2:10 AM ET). Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, in a video message, told US troops to “stay the course,” “ignore the noise,” and finish “what we have started” (Iran International, 10:30 PM ET Saturday). A senior Emirati official, Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, told Fox News Digital he saw some progress in US–Iran talks through Qatari mediation but said renewed confrontation remained possible: “We plan for the worst. We hope for the best” (Iran International, 9:39 PM ET Saturday). Gulf stock markets opened Sunday lower as investors waited for signs of whether Trump would order fresh attacks on Iran (Reuters, 5:30 AM ET).

item.description:
Top line

The U.S. expanded its Iran blockade on land and at sea, CENTCOM said it disabled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, and Iran's IRGC Navy claimed two tankers hit mines near Hormuz as unexplained blasts were reported around Qeshm Island. In Israel, President Isaac Herzog said he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, a setback for Benjamin Netanyahu. In Ukraine, Zelenskyy accused Moscow of intensifying strikes to pressure Kyiv ahead of Nov. 10 talks in Abu Dhabi, where Russia said it will send a senior diplomat. Elsewhere, Houthi authorities blamed Saudi airstrikes for 27 deaths near Sanaa, heavy rain flooded tents across Gaza, and France saw another day of protests. Covers roughly 7 AM through 7 PM ET Saturday, Nov 7.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Blockade and the M/V Huda. Reuters reported exclusively that the U.S. military is launching a CENTCOM task force to restrict Iran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned goods across its land borders and the Caspian Sea, expanding a months-long naval blockade (Reuters, 8:45 AM ET; Iran International, 8:41 AM ET). CENTCOM said Admiral Brad Cooper ordered Task Force Iron Gate, a team of about 20 military and civilian personnel based in Tampa. Later Saturday, CENTCOM said a U.S. military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman, disabling it after the civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and tried several times to breach the blockade; the ship had visited an Iranian port. CENTCOM said it had redirected 147 commercial vessels since July and disabled five that refused to comply, and that U.S. forces had previously destroyed 10 Iranian commercial oil tankers it linked to an IRGC shadow network (CENTCOM, 3:37 PM ET; Iran International, 3:55 PM ET).
  • Hormuz tankers. The IRGC Navy said Saturday that two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire in and near the Strait of Hormuz after using unauthorized routes and switching off their navigation systems—one in the eastern part of the strait and the other inside the waterway. It warned that ships cooperating with the U.S. military or ignoring Iran's restrictions risk hitting mines in prohibited areas. The statement gave no names, flags, cargo details, or casualty information, and there is no independent confirmation; treat this as Iran's account (Iran International, 4:16 PM ET).
  • Qeshm blasts. Iranian state media reported explosions Saturday on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, and IRNA said there were two blasts in eastern Qeshm. State TV said similar sounds were also heard in Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas; a reporter suggested they might be related to Iranian operations to defend the strait. The cause was initially unknown. IRGC-linked Tasnim later cited a source saying the Qeshm explosions were not related to missile strikes (Iran International, 2:38 PM ET; more, 3:25 PM ET; Tasnim, 3:40 PM ET).
  • Diplomacy and signaling. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told President Trump in a Saturday phone call that Ankara would keep working to ease U.S.–Iran tensions through diplomacy, Erdogan's office said (Iran International, 12:55 PM ET). Iran's ambassador to Moscow said security chief Mohsen Rezaei delivered a message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei during a three-hour Kremlin meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday covering U.S. and Israeli attacks, Tehran's conditions for reopening Hormuz, and nuclear cooperation, along with plans for Russian gas supplies to Iran (Iran International, 11:45 AM ET). Rezaei also publicly questioned who in Washington should receive Tehran's warning against another war, pointing to what he called turmoil in the Trump administration after the midterms (Iran International, 10:47 AM ET). Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking Friday at a CPAC event at Mar-a-Lago, said Trump confronted Iran rather than leave the issue to future presidents and called Tehran “the most radical, terroristic regime on the planet” (Iran International, 5:25 PM ET).
  • Missiles, medicines, and the nuclear file. Ali Balali, an adviser to the IRGC Aerospace Force commander, said Saturday that Iran's missiles can strike targets with precision at ranges of about 2,000 kilometers, citing IRNA (Iran International, 1:43 PM ET). Iran's mission to the UN in Vienna accused Washington of using its Rewards for Justice program to recruit help for attacks on Iranian nuclear scientists and facilities, and warned that anyone providing information, including the IAEA, could face legal consequences (Iran International, 2:34 PM ET). Food and Drug Administration spokesman Mohammad Hashemi said Iran is facing supply difficulties for about 40 of its roughly 700 vital and essential medicines (Iran International, 4:33 PM ET). Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Iraq had lost about $60 billion from the halt in Hormuz oil exports and had resumed shipments after understandings with Washington and Tehran (Iran International, 11:23 AM ET).
  • Israel's next government. Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, said he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after last week's election (AP, 2:58 PM ET; BBC, 4:54 PM ET; AFP, 5:45 PM ET). The President's Residence said Eisenkot, who chairs the Yashar party, will formally receive the mandate Sunday at 5 p.m. Israel time (10 a.m. ET) and will then have 28 days to try to assemble a coalition (Times of Israel, 3:06 PM ET).
  • Pahlavi in Frankfurt. Exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi accepted the Friedrich Naumann Foundation's Freedom Prize on behalf of the Iranian people in Frankfurt, a ceremony AFP said critics called illegitimate. Pahlavi said he favored a “third path” of maximum pressure on the Islamic Republic and maximum support for Iranians, and argued that military intervention against the regime's “machinery of repression” had become necessary. Videos sent to Iran International showed demonstrators in the city chanting “Long live the Shah” (AFP, 1:15 PM ET; Iran International, 10:46 AM ET; rally, 8:41 AM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Kyiv and the grid. Zelenskyy said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles overnight, all aimed at Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, and struck substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants with the capital and central Ukraine. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern Bridge is closed in both directions after damage to the roadbed, trolleybus wires, and power lines, and that at least six people were injured in the city, including a 14-year-old girl; a kindergarten and a residential building were also hit. Reuters said the strikes strained power and heating as temperatures headed toward freezing. Russia said it hit targets in and around Kyiv. Zelenskyy accused Moscow of intensifying attacks to pressure Kyiv at upcoming talks (Kyiv Independent, 8:51 AM ET; Reuters, 9:00 AM ET; AFP, 10:25 AM ET; Reuters, 1:10 PM ET).
  • Talks. Zelenskyy said a humanitarian evacuation of civilians from Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast showed a ceasefire can be arranged quickly, and that the main obstacle is Putin's political will. Talks in Abu Dhabi are expected Nov. 10 among Ukrainian, Russian, and U.S. officials. Russia said it will send senior diplomats and military officials, including Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov, who oversees relations with the United States and arms control and will join the negotiations for the first time (Kyiv Independent, 11:51 AM ET; Ryabkov, 5:12 PM ET).
  • Ukraine's strikes and aid. Ukraine's General Staff said it struck Russian Iskander missile launchers and air-defense systems in Bryansk Oblast; these are Ukrainian claims and have not been independently verified (Kyiv Independent, 7:48 AM ET). German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Germany cannot provide Ukraine with more Patriot systems for now and called on other countries to do more (Kyiv Independent, 2:43 PM ET). Ukraine's military intelligence named Russian personnel and said four Su-34 fighter-bombers took part in the deadly strike on an aid center in Komyshuvakha; that identification is a Ukrainian allegation (Kyiv Independent, 7:09 AM ET).
  • Hybrid pressure and casualty claims. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed solidarity with Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani after a cyberattack he said was tied to Italy's stance on Ukraine; Italian media reported she linked it to pro-Russian hackers (Kyiv Independent, 10:55 AM ET). Hackers claimed leaked records from Russia's statistics agency show up to 450,000 war-related deaths from February 2022 through August 2026; this is an unverified claim by the hacking groups (Kyiv Independent, 3:27 PM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen. The Houthi-run health ministry said airstrikes it blamed on Saudi Arabia killed 27 people and wounded 36 in a village near Sanaa, in one of the deadliest reported attacks since fighting resumed in July; Saudi Arabia has not been independently confirmed as the attacker in the reporting cited here (Reuters, 3:00 PM ET). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had carried out six missile and drone operations against oil and military sites in Saudi Arabia and Yemen, Al Jazeera reported; those claims are unverified (Iran International, 12:19 PM ET). Multiple Yemeni officials told AFP that thousands of Syrian troops were set to deploy to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with some already on the ground. A Syrian diplomatic source later told state news agency SANA that Syria has no plans to send troops to Yemen, while saying military cooperation with Saudi Arabia could expand (AFP, 10:00 AM ET; Reuters, 3:50 PM ET).
  • Gaza. Heavy rain flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced people across Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, soaking bedding and leaving many without shelter. Municipal and civil-defense officials said fuel shortages and damaged equipment hampered the response; storms also hit parts of the Israeli coast (Reuters, 10:10 AM ET; Times of Israel, 10:28 AM ET; AFP, 3:30 PM ET).

Other world news

  • France. Thousands protested across France on Saturday against the government and the cost of living. Paris police moved to block an unauthorized gathering near the Élysée Palace, while hundreds later gathered in Place de la République with music and placards backing the student-led movement. Reuters later reported that a police officer's home in France was destroyed by fire, according to the interior minister (AFP, 11:12 AM ET; Reuters, 12:20 PM ET; Reuters, 5:20 PM ET).
  • Paraguay. After Friday's impeachment and the swearing-in of Pedro Alliana, former president Santiago Peña appeared before prosecutors in Asunción and was charged with breach of trust and administration for personal gain. He remains under house arrest in a crisis tied to the collapse of digital bank ueno; protesters gathered outside his home (Reuters, 3:00 PM ET; Reuters, 9:40 AM ET).
  • New Zealand. There was still no clear winner after a tight general election. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said his right-wing coalition had a path back to office but conceded the race remained too close to call (BBC, 10:01 AM ET; AFP, 7:57 AM ET).
  • Indonesia. Workers rallied in support of President Prabowo while women marched against him (Reuters, 9:00 AM ET).

Ali Balali, an adviser to the IRGC Aerospace Force commander, said Saturday that Iran's missiles can strike targets with precision at ranges of about 2,000 kilometers, citing IRNA (Iran International, 1:43 PM ET). Iran's mission to the UN in Vienna accused Washington of using its Rewards for Justice program to recruit help for attacks on Iranian nuclear scientists and facilities, and warned that anyone providing information, including the IAEA, could face legal consequences (Iran International, 2:34 PM ET). Food and Drug Administration spokesman Mohammad Hashemi said Iran is facing supply difficulties for about 40 of its roughly 700 vital and essential medicines (Iran International, 4:33 PM ET). Municipal and civil-defense officials said fuel shortages and damaged equipment hampered the response; storms also hit parts of the Israeli coast (Reuters, 10:10 AM ET; Times of Israel, 10:28 AM ET; AFP, 3:30 PM ET).

Paris police moved to block an unauthorized gathering near the Élysée Palace, while hundreds later gathered in Place de la République with music and placards backing the student-led movement. Reuters later reported that a police officer's home in France was destroyed by fire, according to the interior minister (AFP, 11:12 AM ET; Reuters, 12:20 PM ET; Reuters, 5:20 PM ET).
  • Paraguay. After Friday's impeachment and the swearing-in of Pedro Alliana, former president Santiago Peña appeared before prosecutors in Asunción and was charged with breach of trust and administration for personal gain. He remains under house arrest in a crisis tied to the collapse of digital bank ueno; protesters gathered outside his home (Reuters, 3:00 PM ET; Reuters, 9:40 AM ET).
  • New Zealand. There was still no clear winner after a tight general election. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said his right-wing coalition had a path back to office but conceded the race remained too close to call (BBC, 10:01 AM ET; AFP, 7:57 AM ET).
  • Indonesia. Workers rallied in support of President Prabowo while women marched against him (Reuters, 9:00 AM ET).
