item.description:
Top line

Overnight, Iran's navy said a tanker hit a mine and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, Iranian officials said early-morning blasts near Isfahan were controlled demolitions of leftover ordnance, and Qatar said its U.S.–Iran mediation continues while Trump claimed "a lot of progress." In Ukraine, Russian ballistic missiles damaged Kyiv's Northern Bridge and hit substations linking nuclear plants to the grid, while Ukraine struck the Saratov refinery ahead of next week's Abu Dhabi talks. Elsewhere, ISW flagged a possible Houthi buildup toward Aden, Paraguay swore in a new president after Peña's impeachment, and New Zealand's election is too close to call. Covers roughly 7 PM ET Friday through 7 AM ET Saturday, Nov 7.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Hormuz tanker. Iran's navy said Saturday that an oil tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz after entering an area Tehran had declared off-limits, saying it ignored warnings and switched off its navigation systems (Iran International, 5:03 AM ET). The tanker's name, flag, cargo, and crew status have not been released, and there is no independent confirmation yet—treat this as Iran's account only (X news summary).
  • Isfahan blasts. At least four powerful explosions were felt near Isfahan around 1:49 AM ET, near military sites hit in earlier U.S.–Israeli strikes. Iranian officials and local media called them scheduled controlled detonations of unexploded ordnance; online claims of a new U.S. attack are unsupported so far (X news summary). Reuters late Friday again cited Tasnim saying two missiles struck Qeshm Island (Reuters, 10:30 PM ET). Viral videos of huge tank fires billed as U.S. strikes on Iran actually appear to show a Ukrainian drone strike on Russia's Afipsky refinery, according to X fact-checking summaries (X news summary).
  • Talks. Qatar said its mediation between Washington and Tehran continues and is aimed at preventing escalation, and it denied social-media claims that the talks had collapsed (Reuters, 4:00 AM ET; X news summary). Trump said the U.S. has made "a lot of progress" on Iran, does not consider the confrontation a war, and said U.S. forces destroyed an Iranian-made air-defense system within minutes (Iran International, 3:56 AM ET). Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he spoke with 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours, urging regional security without outside interference (Iran International, 2:25 AM ET). Hardline lawmakers pushed back: Abbas Golrou said negotiating is pointless because the U.S. "wants to take everything and give nothing," and Mahmoud Nabavian demanded changes to Iran's negotiating team (Golrou, 3:55 AM ET; Nabavian, 6:18 AM ET).
  • Threats and nuclear signaling. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the Guards would unveil previously undisclosed capabilities if a third round of fighting broke out, and would make "necessary preparations" if leaders changed Iran's nuclear doctrine (Iran International, 1:47 AM ET; nuclear doctrine, 2:43 AM ET). Lawmaker Ghasem Ravanbakhsh threatened infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and Europe if they back renewed strikes (Iran International, 3:02 AM ET). Reports of iodine-tablet distribution near nuclear sites continue, though Iran's Health Ministry has denied the official's comments behind the story (X news summary). Lebanese lawmaker Alain Aoun warned renewed U.S.–Iran fighting could drag Lebanon back into war (Iran International, 4:50 AM ET).
  • Inside Iran and the diaspora. Iran executed Baluch militant Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh over an attack on a police station in Sistan-Baluchestan (Reuters, 4:20 AM ET). Rights group HRANA said a Tehran court sentenced January protester Hossein Darabi to 25 years for "cooperating with hostile states" (Iran International, 6:58 AM ET). Exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi accepted Germany's Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Prize on behalf of the Iranian people in Frankfurt as large crowds rallied in the city (Iran International, 6:28 AM ET). Iran International also repeated Israel's Channel 12 report that Netanyahu and the Mossad chief planned and then dropped a pre-election Iran operation after an operative's error tipped off Washington—still anonymous sourcing with no official confirmation (Iran International, 5:13 AM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Kyiv strike. Hours after Zelenskyy's warning, Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv overnight, damaging the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro and injuring five people, including a 14-year-old girl, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said (Kyiv Independent, 12:26 AM ET). X summaries citing Ukrainian officials put the attack at up to 36 ballistic missiles and more than 170 drones, with a kindergarten and homes damaged and power, heat, and water outages in the capital—treat the exact counts as preliminary (X news summary).
  • Grid damage. Zelenskyy said Russian attacks over the past day killed 2 and injured 37 across Ukraine and damaged substations connecting nuclear power plants to the grid in the Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv, and Dnipro oblasts (Kyiv Independent, 6:27 AM ET). Germany and Spain are sending generators and repair aid, according to X summaries (X news summary).
  • Ukraine's strikes. Ukraine hit sites in Russia's Oryol, Saratov, and Rostov regions overnight, including the Saratov oil refinery, according to monitoring channels (Kyiv Independent, 10:14 PM ET). Ukraine's General Staff claimed 2,280 Russian personnel losses in the past day; these are Ukrainian estimates, not independently verified (Kyiv Independent, 3:18 AM ET).
  • Talks ahead. ISW said U.S. officials are presenting a list of topics, including security guarantees and European security architecture, for the upcoming Abu Dhabi negotiations, and assessed that Russia's stated demands undercut U.S., Ukrainian, and European positions (ISW, 9:07 PM ET; more, 10:00 PM ET). EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas rejected giving Moscow a say in Europe's security after Jared Kushner outlined a broader U.S. framework (X news summary). ISW also flagged an unattributed campaign of hoax bomb threats targeting European flights, airports, and media (ISW, 10:30 PM ET). Elon Musk reposted a post calling SpaceX's free Starlink service to Ukraine early in the war "a mistake" (Kyiv Independent, 7:08 PM ET).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen. ISW assessed that the Houthis may be massing forces in al Turbah, on the Taiz–Aden road, ahead of a large offensive into Lahij Governorate and toward Aden (ISW, 11:20 PM ET). ISW also said the Houthis' new "transit permits" for Bab al Mandeb shipping set a precedent of armed groups controlling global chokepoints (ISW, 9:44 PM ET). Houthi-posted videos claim captures in the Kahboub mountains overlooking the strait; these are unverified (X news summary). Blame for Friday's deadly Taiz market strike remains disputed (X news summary).
  • Haiti. Haiti's prime minister said gang leader Mathias Saintil is dead (Reuters, 12:50 AM ET).
  • Gaza and the UN. Debate continued over the UN's choice of American Luke Lindberg to lead the World Food Programme amid deep aid cuts in Gaza (X news summary).

Other world news

  • Paraguay. After the Senate impeached Santiago Peña, he was placed under house arrest and Alliana was sworn in as president (Reuters, 12:10 AM ET; Reuters, 1:40 AM ET).
  • New Zealand. The two main parties were neck and neck with over half the votes counted; the prime minister said he sees a "pathway" to forming the next government but called it too close to call (AFP, 4:35 AM ET; AFP, 6:27 AM ET).
  • Asia. Malaysia's king warned against challenging his order allowing house arrest for ex-PM Najib (Reuters, 2:00 AM ET). Hong Kong lawmakers condemned foreign criticism of the Joshua Wong ruling (Reuters, 1:00 AM ET). Indonesian workers rallied for Prabowo as women marched against him (Reuters, 4:50 AM ET). Delhi was ranked the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali (Reuters, 12:40 AM ET).
  • Europe and Africa. French unions and students plan another day of protests Saturday, with a banned Yellow Vests rally also planned in Paris (AFP, 5:05 AM ET). A Kenyan court sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years over the Shakahola starvation deaths (X news summary).
  • United States. Reuters reported exclusively that Rubio is seeking to impose order at the State Department as Republicans look to 2028 (Reuters, 6:20 AM ET). AFP framed Stephen Miller's appointment as chief of staff as a "bare-knuckle fightback" after the midterms (AFP, 5:29 AM ET). CAIR suspended its Florida operations over a state "terrorist" designation law (Reuters, 11:00 PM ET). The Nasdaq rebounded Friday but posted a fourth straight weekly decline (Reuters, 12:30 AM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 6, PM
item.description:
Top line

Friday evening, Trump said U.S. talks with Iran were going well even as Reuters reported two missiles struck Iran’s Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. embassies warned of Iranian plots against officials, and reports of iodine distribution near Iranian nuclear sites continued. In Ukraine, Zelenskyy warned of a major Russian attack on energy and Dnipro bridges as ballistic missiles hit Kyiv, Putin confirmed trilateral Abu Dhabi talks for Nov 10–11, and the Komyshuvakha aid-site death toll held at 53. Elsewhere, a Yemen market strike killed dozens with conflicting blame, Reuters said Syria is advising Saudi forces against the Houthis, and Paraguay’s Senate impeached President Santiago Peña. Covers roughly 7 AM ET through 7 PM ET Friday, Nov 6.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Talks and Qeshm. Trump told reporters the U.S. is in productive talks with Iranian representatives, stressing no U.S. soldier losses in months and an open Strait of Hormuz with steady oil flow—comments that came as Qatar’s prime minister said six months of mediation had not produced a full agreement (X news summary; related). Reuters reported Iranian outlet Tasnim saying two missiles struck Iran’s Qeshm Island (Reuters, 6:20 PM ET). Separate X news summaries described overnight blasts and air-defense activity there, with Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claiming they downed a U.S. MQ-1 drone and U.S. officials describing a fighter-jet strike on an Iranian missile launcher; both sides framed the actions as limited and said shipping was not disrupted—treat tactical detail as contested (X news summary).
  • Strike options and alerts. After national-security meetings Wednesday and Thursday, Trump kept military, sanctions, and diplomatic options on the table and said the world would know his choice soon; some reporting linked possible timing to around Nov 9’s new moon—treat that schedule as unconfirmed (X news summary; related). Late Friday, U.S. embassies in Jerusalem, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and Bahrain urged heightened vigilance over intelligence on Iranian efforts to target senior U.S. officials and Houthi attack risks; no attacks were reported in those alerts (X news summary). Reports continued that Iranian authorities distributed iodine tablets near nuclear sites and that Iraq kept nuclear-emergency monitoring and airspace limits Nov 7–11; Iranian state media has denied the iodine story (X news summary).
  • Hormuz, Russia, and cables. An Iranian lawmaker said commercial vessels from India, China, Iraq, and Qatar can pass the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian interference despite broader restrictions, with transit fees tied to imports and political support for some partners (X news summary). X news summaries said Iran’s Mohsen Rezaei met Putin seeking S-400 systems and other support after earlier damage to Iranian air defenses; no finalized sale was confirmed and Ukraine commitments constrain Moscow (X news summary). Maritime firm Windward continued to flag Iran-linked vessels loitering near Gulf of Oman undersea cables after IRGC warnings; no cable damage has been confirmed (X news summary). Reuters separately said the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Canadian money-services firms over Iran-related transactions (Reuters, 4:10 PM ET).
  • Politics and Israel. Vice President JD Vance again blamed the Iran war for GOP midterm losses, drawing loyalty criticism from pro-Israel voices while Trump defended the campaign (X news summary). Progressive Democrats including Sen. Chris Van Hollen pushed to bar Iran-war funding in any spending bill before the Dec 11 deadline; former counterterrorism official Joe Kent publicly urged Trump to end the war and fire several top aides (X news summary; Kent). Israeli Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu and Mossad chief Roman Gofman prepared a covert Iran operation before the Oct 27 Israeli election that the U.S. blocked after an operative error—anonymous sourcing, no official confirmation from Jerusalem or Washington (X news summary). Avigdor Liberman signaled willingness to compromise on Haredi draft exemptions to help form an anti-Netanyahu government as coalition talks continued (X news summary). Iranian lawmakers again warned of missile strikes on European bases if the U.S. resumes attacks; analysts note range and political limits on such threats (X news summary).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Kyiv under fire. Kyiv Independent reports several waves of Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv Friday evening after Zelenskyy warned partners of intelligence on a major strike against energy infrastructure, Dnipro River bridges, and civilian sites, and urged more Patriot missiles. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russia was hitting infrastructure near the capital (Kyiv Independent, 6:27 PM ET; Zelenskyy warning, 3:23 PM ET). Rolling blackouts continued as winter cold set in (X news summary).
  • Civilian sites and Komyshuvakha. X news summaries said Russian Geran-2 and Shahed drones struck a hospital in Izium, Kharkiv region, injuring civilians and cutting power for more than 13,000 people, while staff at Chernivtsi’s children’s hospice evacuated terminally ill children during nearby air raids (X news summary). The death toll from the Nov 2 Russian strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, remained at 53 as the search entered a fifth day (Kyiv Independent, 2:10 PM ET; X news summary).
  • Abu Dhabi talks. Putin confirmed trilateral Russia–U.S.–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10–11, with Russia’s Vladimir Medinsky leading Moscow’s team; Kyiv Independent said Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine’s delegation despite earlier media confusion. Agenda items cited include security guarantees, de-escalation, and humanitarian issues; Ukrainian adviser Kyrylo Budanov has called the meeting progress without expecting breakthroughs (X news summary; Kyiv Independent, 4:26 PM ET). Coverage of Melania Trump’s White House ceremony marking the Oleshky local ceasefire and evacuation of nearly 800 civilians continued (X news summary).
  • Aid, ISW, and diplomacy. A top Zelenskyy ally said midterm results “doubled” Ukraine’s chances of U.S. military aid (Kyiv Independent, 5:11 PM ET). ISW assessed that Russian and occupation authorities are using patronage links between Russian regions and occupied Ukrainian cities to facilitate “holidays” that temporarily deport Ukrainian children (ISW, 4:35 PM ET). NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in a Dutch TV interview that the war will end in compromise with Ukraine deciding its terms, and that Russia will remain a threat to Europe afterward (X news summary). Claims linking Zelenskyy vehicles to a NABU cash seizure remain unverified and are not confirmed by NABU updates (X news summary).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen. A strike hit Al-Hadara Popular Market in Al-Wazi’yah district Friday, with preliminary reports of about 20–30 civilians killed and a similar number wounded; Houthi officials blamed a Saudi F-15, while Yemeni government sources and Al Arabiya blamed a Houthi ballistic missile—blame remains contested (X news summary). The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a drone aimed at the Makkah area during Friday prayers with no casualties reported (X news summary). item.title: World News Brief: Nov 6, AM
item.description:
Top line

Overnight, Trump kept Iran options on the table after national-security meetings, saying he would “rather not destroy the rest” of Iran but “maybe will have to,” while Tehran warned it could fire on Europe if U.S. strikes came from European bases and oil prices firmed again on Hormuz risk. Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Trump on next steps. Times of Israel reports President Trump said after security meetings he would “rather not destroy the rest” of Iran but “maybe will have to,” with a decision coming soon (Times of Israel, 12:26 AM ET). Separate X news summaries say Central Command laid out strike, pressure, and deal options and that Trump told reporters he is “locked and loaded” if needed; treat operational detail as unconfirmed (X news summary; related). Trump also framed the months-long campaign as a “virtual occupation” with low U.S. casualties compared with past wars—an characterization that drew mixed online reaction (X news summary).
  • Iran threats and cables. Iranian lawmakers on the parliament security committee warned that U.S. strikes launched from European bases could draw Iranian missiles toward Italy, Germany, and other host countries; treat the rhetoric as threat messaging, not a confirmed launch order (X news summary). Maritime firm Windward tracked Iran-linked vessels loitering over undersea cable routes in the Gulf of Oman after IRGC warnings that such links could be targeted if new U.S.–Israeli strikes begin; no sabotage has been confirmed (X news summary).
  • Oil and Hormuz. Brent climbed back toward the $100 area Friday as traders priced renewed escalation risk after midterm-driven swings; X news summaries put prices near about $99.90 after an earlier selloff (X news summary). Earlier Iranian claims of tanker hits and drone shootdowns near Hormuz remain without U.S. confirmation (X news summary).
  • Carrier and Iraq. Open-source trackers say the USS Theodore Roosevelt is stopping in Singapore en route toward Central Command, with arrival in the theater not expected before mid-November; that timing is not an official strike schedule (X news summary). Iraq’s civil aviation authority kept airspace limits for military activity Nov 7–11 over major airports and activated nuclear-emergency monitoring along the Iran border, citing low fallout risk (X news summary). Sirens at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on Nov 5 were later assessed as an early-warning test, not an incoming attack (X news summary).
  • Politics and aid. Israel’s UN ambassador Danny Danon told i24NEWS the late-February 2026 decision to strike Iran was America’s alone and that Israel is unfairly blamed for war-driven U.S. gas prices (X news summary). Trump said he and Netanyahu agreed to end roughly $4 billion a year in U.S. military aid by year’s end, framing Israel as strong enough to buy weapons itself; analysts note Congress may still have to act on the 2016 MOU through 2028 (X news summary; related). In Israel’s government-formation talks, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot led Netanyahu in Knesset recommendations (about 67 to 46) ahead of President Herzog’s mandate decision; coalition arithmetic remains unsettled (X news summary).
  • Rights case. Iran’s Revolutionary Court sentenced activist Amirhossein Mousavi to death for “corruption on earth” tied to posts on X, plus a separate prison term for insulting religious sanctities; family and rights advocates say a televised confession was coerced and are seeking international pressure to halt the execution (X news summary).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Komyshuvakha at 53. Kyiv Independent reports the death toll from the Nov 2 Russian strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, has risen to 53 as the search enters a fifth day—the deadliest Russian attack on that oblast since the full-scale invasion began. Russia says it hit military targets; Ukraine and the UN emphasize the civilian aid gathering (Kyiv Independent, 6:10 AM ET; X news summary).
  • Blackouts and energy war. Overnight Russian drones and strikes hit energy sites, with outages reported across Kyiv and Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, and Chernihiv regions; some areas faced up to about 19–20 hours without power as winter cold set in (X news summary; related). Ukrainian drones overnight struck the Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar, with large fires reported; Russian authorities blamed falling debris and claimed dozens of drones downed. The hit follows recent strikes on Ryazan and other Russian refining sites (Kyiv Independent, 11:47 PM ET Nov 5; X news summary; ISW).
  • Diplomacy track. Kyiv Independent reports Trump met Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington and claimed a “big, beautiful agreement” is coming ahead of U.S.–Ukraine–Russia working-level talks. Jared Kushner described a U.S. plan for security guarantees and a broader European framework, with trilateral sessions in Abu Dhabi next week after Brussels consultations—details remain unconfirmed and no deal text is public (Kyiv Independent, 9:57 PM ET Nov 5; X news summary). Melania Trump’s White House event marking the Oleshky local ceasefire and evacuation of nearly 800 civilians continued to draw coverage overnight (Kyiv Independent; X news summary).
  • Aid and politics. Zelenskyy said Ukraine has “increased chances” of more U.S. aid after Democrats’ midterm wins and still needs to consolidate bipartisan support; he also thanked Spain for about $490 million focused on air defenses (Kyiv Independent, 7:18 PM ET Nov 5; Spain aid). An X news summary says the EU disbursed about €4.36 billion under its multi-year loan program for budget and defense needs (X news summary). Ukraine’s General Staff put cumulative Russian personnel losses above 1.6 million; those are Ukrainian estimates and are not independently verified (Kyiv Independent, 2:24 AM ET; X news summary).
  • UK and sport. The UK announced a Ukrainian-language GCSE from 2028 for students in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, aimed in part at refugee children (X news summary). The IIHF continues to resist a CAS ruling that would restore Russian teams, while Canada still plans to deny visas for the World Juniors in Alberta (X news summary).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen–Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said air defenses intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles toward Najran and later a drone over the Mecca region; debris damage was under assessment (X news summary). ISW assessed that Houthi demands for Saudi recognition of Houthi sovereignty aim to end Riyadh’s role in the war and clear a path toward controlling all of Yemen; Saudi officials have called a related Wall Street Journal report of a $51 billion demand a “pure fabrication” (ISW; Saudi denial).
  • Sudan and the UAE. Coverage continued of a leaked UN report alleging UAE-linked recruitment of Colombian mercenaries for Sudan’s RSF as Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh courts African Group support for UN secretary-general; she pledges to prioritize ending the war, and the UAE denies arming the RSF (X news summary; related).
  • Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Security forces cleared months-long protests in Rawalakot; protesters and officials give conflicting accounts of who fired first, with at least three named deaths reported and communications blackouts hindering verification (X news summary).

Other world news

  • Flights. AP reports new bomb threats hit European air traffic in at least three incidents, extending a week of hoax alerts; Reuters separately noted a Prague–Rome flight diverted to Venice (AP, 6:18 AM ET; Reuters, 6:00 AM ET).
  • Kenya. AP says the leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult linked to more than 400 deaths was sentenced to 200 years in prison (AP, 7:01 AM ET).
  • Vatican. Reuters reports Vatican officials said Pope Leo is healthy enough for a three-country South America tour less than a month after lung-cancer surgery, with no extra medical precautions planned (Reuters, 6:15 AM ET).
  • Netherlands. Protesters broke into a Microsoft data-center construction site in Amsterdam (Reuters, 5:51 AM ET).
  • Malaysia. Former prime minister Najib Razak’s move toward house arrest for the rest of his 1MDB sentence hit a snag as authorities said a legal review was needed (Reuters, 6:35 AM ET; earlier AP).
  • U.S. domestic. A federal judge temporarily blocked groundbreaking on Trump’s planned memorial arch in Washington for 14 days after a key panel had approved it (AP, 12:26 AM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 5, AM
item.description:
Top line

Overnight, Axios reported the U.S. military is finalizing preparations for possible large-scale operations against Iran even as oil prices slide on hopes the midterm rebuke will curb the war. A tanker was hit by unidentified projectiles north of Qatar, and Iran's IRGC advertised Hormuz readiness. In Ukraine, the Komyshuvakha school-aid strike death toll reached 42, Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Russia's Ryazan oil refinery, and the EU disbursed more than €4 billion in support. Covers roughly 7 PM ET Wednesday, Nov 4, through 7 AM ET Thursday, Nov 5.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • U.S. options and buildup (reported). Axios says the U.S. military is finalizing preparations for major combat against Iran, including regional deployments, with some officials pushing strikes on energy and nuclear sites—possibly with Israel—while Qatari mediators draft a deal to restart talks. No final decision is reported; Vance has privately criticized Netanyahu's Iran approach (X news summary of Axios). Separately, Axios framed Trump's post-midterm Iran choices as mostly bad (Axios, 8:06 PM ET Wed), and Reuters asked whether the election rebuke makes Trump more aggressive or more cautious (Reuters podcast).
  • Oil slides. Reuters says oil is headed for its biggest weekly drop since the pandemic after Democrats took Congress, with Vance blaming the Iran war for the GOP losses (Reuters, 6:30 AM ET; Morning Bid).
  • Iran reads the midterms as a win. ISW says Iranian leaders treat the Nov 3 results as proof their military strategy imposed political costs on Washington and will keep maximalist demands; Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's remarks point the same way (ISW, 8:47 PM ET Wed; follow-up). Tehran billboards and state rallies have threatened Trump and others after the vote (X news summary).
  • Hormuz and Gulf shipping. UK Maritime Trade Operations said a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal around 6:20 PM ET Wed; crew status and damage were unclear (X news summary). Separately, Iranian media showed IRGC Ground Forces commander Brig. Gen. Mohammad Karami inspecting Strait of Hormuz units and vowing a crushing response to any aggression (X news summary). IRGC claims of related Hormuz fires and downed U.S. drones remain unverified. South Korea plans to expand its Cheonghae naval unit near the strait with patrol aircraft and more personnel, pending parliament (X news summary).
  • Russia–Iran arms (reported). Financial Times documents cited in an X news summary describe a 2024–25 Russian plan to produce 90 helicopter-mounted LMUR missile launchers coded for Iran ("K-10"). Delivery is unconfirmed.
  • Iran as space power. Axios reports an intel assessment identifying Iran as an "emerging space power" (Axios, 6:21 AM ET).
  • Israel politics and the war. Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon said in an i24NEWS interview that the decision to attack Iran was America's, with Israel in support (X news summary). United Torah Judaism declined to recommend any PM candidate to President Herzog, withholding backing from Netanyahu (Times of Israel, 3:15 AM ET). Times of Israel also notes the abrupt end of U.S. military aid could shift the relationship (Times of Israel); that aid cutoff still needs clearer wire confirmation on timing and scope.

Russia–Ukraine

  • Komyshuvakha toll at 42. Police say 42 bodies have been recovered from the Nov 2 Russian strike on a school used as an aid point in Zaporizhzhia region, with the search continuing; it is already among the deadliest single attacks of the war (Reuters, 6:20 AM ET; Kyiv Independent).
  • Ryazan refinery hit. A Russian oil refinery in Ryazan, a large Rosneft plant, was reportedly targeted in a drone attack overnight; local officials described fires from debris and at least one injury (Kyiv Independent, 10:38 PM ET Wed; X news summary). Summaries call it the fifth major Russian refinery hit in about a week.
  • Overnight drones. Russian drone attacks injured four people in Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv oblasts and sparked fires at infrastructure, including logistics sites in Kyiv Oblast (Kyiv Independent, 1:05 AM ET). Separately, Kyiv still faces severe power and water risk after recent energy strikes (X news summary), and chronic-illness patients are asking strangers online to mail scarce medicines after strikes on pharma logistics (Kyiv Independent).
  • EU cash. The EU disbursed over €4 billion in budget support to Ukraine (reports put the package around €4.36 billion including defense elements) (Kyiv Independent, 5:56 AM ET; X news summary).
  • Diplomacy. Russia's Kirill Dmitriev is in Washington for the first U.S. contact since Trump's midterm setback (Reuters, 5:35 AM ET). Working-level Ukraine–U.S.–Russia talks remain set for Nov 10–11 in Abu Dhabi. Zelenskyy said in a ZDF interview he hopes a Democratic Congress will strengthen military and financial support (X news summary).
  • Ukrainian loss claims. Ukraine's General Staff estimated about 2,380 Russian personnel killed or wounded in the prior day—among its highest single-day figures; these are Ukrainian estimates without independent verification (Kyiv Independent; X news summary).

Other conflicts

  • Yemen–Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the Medina region (X news summary). Separately, summaries say Houthis have demanded about $51 billion in compensation plus recognition as Yemen's government in peace talks with Riyadh; neither side has publicly confirmed those terms (X news summary). Unverified.
  • West Bank. Israeli forces demolished Palestinian homes in Biddu northwest of Jerusalem during olive-harvest season, with reports of dozens displaced; Israel linked some action to a prior deadly shooting case (X news summary). President Herzog had warned Netanyahu of a "highly explosive" West Bank reality and settler violence (Times of Israel, 11:00 PM ET Wed).
  • Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Security forces cleared long-running protest sit-ins in Rawalakot; local reports claim multiple dead and wounded, while authorities say armed protesters fired first. Independent verification is limited (X news summary). Unconfirmed casualty figures.

Other world news

  • Hong Kong. Democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison on his second conviction under Beijing's national security law (AP, 10:31 PM ET Wed).
  • Europe bomb threats. Multiple flights in Europe were diverted over bomb threats, including a Finnair flight that landed in Rome (AP, 5:37 AM ET; Reuters).
  • France unrest. Strikes and protests continued across France, with students blockading schools and trash fires in Paris, as Macron tries to contain the unrest (Reuters, 6:35 AM ET).
  • Baltic cable case. A Finland court convicted the Fitburg captain and a crew member over Baltic Sea cable damage (Reuters, 5:45 AM ET).
  • China trade. China said U.S. farm purchases hinge on a tariff-cut deal (Reuters, 7:00 AM ET). Nvidia chips are piling up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval, Reuters reported exclusively (Reuters).
  • Canada and World Juniors. Canada barred Russian and Belarusian teams from the World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta while Russia's invasion of Ukraine continues (X news summary).
  • Sports. Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer (AP, 6:12 AM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 4, PM
item.description:
Top line

The day after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, the Iran war dominated Washington's post-mortem: Trump said the war was worth it while admitting it hurt Republicans, and Vice President Vance questioned whether it was worth the cost. Gulf states are reportedly bracing for possible new U.S. strikes on Iran, and the U.S. sanctioned Indian and Turkish firms for aiding Tehran. In Ukraine, Russia's winter strike campaign keeps knocking out power, while Ukraine and its partners prepare for U.S.-brokered talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10–11. Covers roughly 7 AM to 7 PM ET Wednesday, Nov 4.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Trump: the war was worth it. Trump acknowledged the Iran war and high gas prices played a role in Republican midterm losses but said "the Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it" (AP, 3:18 PM ET; Reuters, 3:41 PM ET). AFP reports analysts see few good options for him from here (AFP).
  • Vance distances himself. Reuters reports Vice President JD Vance questioned whether the war was worth the cost and blamed it for the election losses (Reuters, 5:03 PM ET; AP explainer). Republican allies are also pressing Trump to shake up his staff and drop policies including the war and tariffs (Reuters), though Trump publicly backed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth (Reuters).
  • New U.S. sanctions. The U.S. sanctioned Indian and Turkish companies and individuals for aiding Iran (Reuters, 2:10 PM ET).
  • Gulf states bracing (reported). Citing a Wall Street Journal report, an X news summary says U.S. Gulf allies are preparing for possible heavy U.S. airstrikes on Iran, with airport drills in Qatar and the UAE and Patriot systems being moved to Israel. Trump has said no immediate strike is planned. I haven't seen the WSJ report directly.
  • Disputed chemical-weapons warning. Israel has shared intelligence claiming Iran is advancing chemical-weapon delivery, which has reportedly split U.S. officials; some see it as pressure to pull Trump into new strikes, and Iran denies it (X news summary). Unconfirmed.
  • Hormuz exemptions (Iranian claim). An Iranian lawmaker says ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar may now pass the Strait of Hormuz, with Indian and Chinese ships still paying fees (X news summary). Not independently confirmed.
  • Embassy-takeover anniversary rallies. Iranians rallied nationwide on the 47th anniversary of the 1979 U.S. Embassy seizure; Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said U.S. elections won't change American hostility, and some banners urged Iran to quit the NPT (X news summary). Iranian state TV also aired a map showing missile paths to Kyiv, Lviv, Odesa and Rzeszow, Poland; Ukraine's disinformation center called circulating versions altered (X news summary).
  • Israel and the U.S. Reuters says the new Congress and growing Republican unease could bring the biggest reassessment of U.S. support for Israel in decades (Reuters). Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon said the decision to attack Iran was America's, with Israel in support (X news summary). That summary also says Trump announced an end to $4 billion a year in military aid to Israel by the end of 2026; I couldn't confirm that from a wire report, so treat it as unverified. Israeli opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot pledged to renew a bipartisan U.S.-Israel alliance (Times of Israel, 6:53 PM ET).
  • Death sentence over X posts. A Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced activist Amirhossein Mousavi to death over his online posts, according to an X news summary.

Russia–Ukraine

  • Grid under attack. ISW says Russia's overnight Nov 3–4 drone strikes hit central and western Ukraine hardest and caused significant outages nationwide, part of a winter campaign doing serious damage to infrastructure and the economy (ISW, 5:34 PM ET; ISW takeaways). Reports describe Kyiv getting only a few hours of power some days and a missile hitting a hospice in Dnipro (X news summary).
  • Komyshuvakha toll rises. The death toll from Russia's Nov 2 bombing of a school where civilians were collecting aid in Zaporizhzhia region is at least 40, with more possibly under rubble (X news summary).

item.description:
Top line

Democrats took control of both the House and Senate in Tuesday's U.S. midterms, and President Trump said the Iran war was part of the reason. Around the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim four tankers are burning after hitting mines, while Trump says the U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran. In Ukraine, the fallout continues from a massive Russian strike on the power grid, ahead of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Covers roughly 7 PM ET Tuesday to 7 AM ET Wednesday, Nov 4.

Iran and Israel–Iran

  • Tankers reported ablaze near Hormuz (Iranian claim). Reuters reported at 11:00 PM ET Tuesday, and again at 3:10 AM ET, that the IRGC says four tankers caught fire after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz (Reuters). This is Iran's account and hasn't been independently confirmed. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) warned of a tanker struck twice in the engine room about 14 nautical miles off Lima, Oman, around 2 PM ET Tuesday, with no casualties or spills reported, according to an X news summary. The IRGC also claims to have shot down another U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone. That claim is unconfirmed.
  • Trump: no immediate plan to strike Iran. Trump told the Financial Times the U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran (Reuters, 11:40 PM ET).
  • Trump links the Iran war to GOP midterm losses. "I think a part of it was Iran," Trump told Fox News (Reuters, 6:45 AM ET). The Times of Israel quotes him saying "people weren't willing to pay more for gasoline" (Times of Israel).
  • U.S. to end annual aid to Israel. Trump says he made a deal with Netanyahu to stop the roughly $4 billion in yearly U.S. funding to Israel after this year, while continuing weapons sales (Reuters, 10:58 PM ET). AFP puts the figure at $3.8 billion a year (AFP).
  • Selective Hormuz passage. An Iranian lawmaker says ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from Iran's transit restrictions, with Qatari ships passing fee-free, according to an X news summary. That's a lawmaker's statement, not a confirmed government policy. Meanwhile, Reuters reports India's refiner MRPL is buying more delivered oil because of shipping risks (Reuters).
  • Gulf threats hit motorsport. Iran's Fars news agency published a "target" list that names hotels in Doha and Abu Dhabi used by F1 and MotoGP teams. Yamaha has reportedly pulled its MotoGP teams from Qatar, while F1 is keeping its schedule for now, according to an X news summary. These reports aren't confirmed.
  • Inside Iran. Iran executed two men tied to January protests in Isfahan, bringing executions in that case to nine, according to an X news summary. On Wednesday, state-organized rallies marked the anniversary of the 1979 U.S. Embassy seizure (X news summary). Billboards in Tehran threatening Trump were also reported.
  • Israeli politics. President Herzog accepted the certified results of the Oct. 27 election and will begin consultations on forming a government (AP, 5:57 AM ET). Israel's electoral authorities rejected Netanyahu's allegations of fraud by Arab parties (AFP, 5:55 AM ET).

Russia–Ukraine

  • Grid strike fallout. ISW describes the large combined drone and missile strike on Ukrainian energy infrastructure overnight Nov 2–3 as part of a campaign to coerce Ukraine (ISW, 12:05 AM ET). According to an X news summary, power plants were damaged in several regions, a hospice in Dnipro was hit (nearly 50 patients evacuated), and civilian deaths reached about 38. The same summary says Kyiv is down to about 2.5 hours of power a day. Those casualty and outage figures haven't been checked against a wire report.
  • Ukrainian strikes inside Russia. Online retailer Ozon says a drone hit one of its logistics centers in Russia's Adygea Republic overnight (Kyiv Independent). The Russian-run management of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant says a Ukrainian drone killed two people, including a station employee (Reuters, 7:45 PM ET). That claim comes from the Russian side only.
  • Diplomacy. In Berlin with Chancellor Merz, Zelensky said there's no point in talks with Putin without a ceasefire first. U.S.-brokered talks are set for Abu Dhabi on Nov 10–11 (X news summary). Britain and France are preparing a post-ceasefire stabilization force, which will rehearse in Exercise Koalicja in Poland from Nov 9–22 (X news summary).
  • Other items. Zelensky awarded Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga for humanitarian work (Kyiv Independent). Canada will block Russia from the World Junior Hockey Championship despite a court ruling (Kyiv Independent). Ukraine's military estimates 2,180 Russian personnel losses in the past day (Kyiv Independent). That's a Ukrainian figure that can't be independently verified.

U.S. midterms (world impact)

  • Democrats will control both chambers of Congress (Reuters). Closer to home, Reuters reports Democrat Annie Andrews won South Carolina's U.S. Senate seat in an upset (Reuters, 5:50 AM ET).
  • Other notable upsets include Gina Hinojosa defeating Texas Gov. Abbott (Reuters) and Adam Hamilton beating Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas (AP). Keisha Lance Bottoms was projected to win Georgia's governor race (Reuters).

Other world news

  • Indonesia's president fired his chief of staff over alleged wiretapping (Reuters, 6:35 AM ET).
  • The Philippines and China pledged to keep talking despite tensions in the South China Sea (Reuters).
  • Oracle dropped a $7 billion AI deal with Tencent under pressure from Trump, the FT reports (Reuters).
  • The International Court of Justice will rule on Nov 19 in The Gambia's Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar (X news summary).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 3, PM
item.description:
Iran and the Gulf

Trump: no immediate plan to strike. President Trump told the Financial Times the U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran (Reuters, 7:00 PM ET). That follows overnight U.S. strikes on Qeshm Island, which a U.S. official described as limited and not a resumption of major combat operations; Fox News, citing officials, called them defensive (Times of Israel, 9:00 AM ET).

Talks: Tehran says no deal is near. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on state TV that message exchanges through Qatari mediators continue with no new steps toward agreement, and security official Mohsen Rezaei called the U.S. response to Iran's seven conditions unconvincing, demanding they be met before the Strait of Hormuz reopens (X story summary). Earlier reports said the U.S. had approved a Qatari-brokered draft trading nuclear concessions for the release of some frozen funds; that draft is reported, not officially confirmed (X story summary).

IRGC warning and threats. The Revolutionary Guard said it is carrying out Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's directives for "maximum deterrence," with updated target lists and responses "without geographic limits"; Italy urged its citizens to leave Iran immediately (X story summary). Iran's Fars news agency published a "target" list that included hotels in Doha and Abu Dhabi used by Formula 1 and MotoGP teams; Yamaha reportedly pulled its MotoGP teams from Qatar, while F1 says its races remain scheduled (X story summary). A billboard in Tehran's Revolution Square shows Trump behind bars with the words "We Will Kill Trump" (X story summary).

Israeli chemical-weapons warning (disputed). Israel has reportedly told U.S. officials that Iran may use chemical weapons, but some U.S. and Gulf officials are skeptical of the evidence and Iran denies it. Reports that U.S. strike options could be ready as early as Nov. 4 are unconfirmed (X story summary).

Drone near Minab (unconfirmed). Footage showed drone wreckage near Minab, which Iranian sources first called a downed U.S. Switchblade. Analysts say it more likely matches an Iranian one-way attack drone, possibly hit by friendly fire; neither government has commented (X story summary).

  • Trump said the U.S. will stop providing its roughly $4 billion a year in military aid to Israel after year-end, saying he and Netanyahu agreed to it months ago (Times of Israel, 9:51 AM ET; BBC, 10:12 AM ET).
  • Reuters reports, citing eight sources, that U.S. intelligence sharing on Iran and other threats with Congress and across the government has slowed and at times stopped during Trump's second term (Reuters, 12:38 PM ET).
  • Oil fell more than 5% Tuesday after Iran's denial, following a 7% drop Monday (X story summary). Gulf oil flows dipped in October from their post-war high (Reuters, 3:00 PM ET).
  • The German Freedom Prize going to "the Iranian people," to be accepted by Reza Pahlavi in Frankfurt on Nov. 7, has drawn opposition from more than 300 Iranian diaspora groups (X story summary).

Russia–Ukraine

Komyshuvakha toll rises to 33. Zelensky said in Berlin that 33 people were killed in Russian strikes on a school used as an aid center in Zaporizhzhia region, and more than 50 may still be trapped under rubble, calling it one of Moscow's worst attacks of the war (Kyiv Independent, 3:25 PM ET; AFP, 5:00 PM ET). Russian attacks across Ukraine killed 38 and injured 158 overall, including morning missile strikes on Dnipro hospitals (Kyiv Independent, 7:37 AM ET; BBC, 11:40 AM ET). Kyiv is reported to have rolling outages leaving about 2.5 hours of power a day (X story summary).

Diplomacy. Standing with Chancellor Merz, Zelensky said talks with Putin are pointless without a ceasefire first (X story summary). The European Commission hosts talks in Brussels on Nov. 4 with the U.S., Ukraine, NATO and European states to coordinate ahead of planned talks with Russia (Kyiv Independent, 11:45 AM ET), and U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi remain set for Nov. 10–11. Melania Trump will host Ukrainian and Russian officials at the White House over the Oleshky evacuation ceasefire she helped broker (Kyiv Independent, 9:02 AM ET). In Minsk, Lukashenko predicted the war will end in coming months, while Lavrov rejected limited truces (X story summary).

  • Ukraine charged Zelensky's former press secretary Iuliia Mendel with treason (Kyiv Independent, 12:35 PM ET).
  • Norway is deploying more NASAMS air-defense sensors and troops to Finnmark on the Russian border (Kyiv Independent, 4:30 PM ET).
  • Britain and France lead a planned post-ceasefire force; about 2,800 personnel from 11 nations exercise in Poland Nov. 9–22 (X story summary).
  • Several Russian regions have sharply cut extra payments to families of fallen soldiers, per Meduza and analysts (X story summary). Russian utility bills are up more than 50% since 2022 (Reuters, 1:01 PM ET).
  • Allegations of abuse at a holding site for mobilized men near Kyiv continue to circulate; Budanov said "outside influence" played a role in the unrest. Many claims are unverified (Kyiv Independent, 2:43 PM ET; X story summary).

Other Conflicts and Security

  • Israeli ex-generals are condemning settler violence and helping Palestinian farmers in the West Bank (Reuters, 5:45 PM ET).
  • The World Court will rule in the Rohingya genocide case on Nov. 19 (Reuters, 5:50 PM ET).
  • North Korea denied a Binance-related accusation and refused dialogue with Washington (Reuters, 6:00 PM ET).
  • ISW says China's navy may soon commission the Sichuan, an amphibious assault ship with an electromagnetic catapult (ISW, 2:24 PM ET).
  • Bomb threats disrupted flights across Europe (Reuters, 5:35 PM ET).

Top World News

U.S. midterms. The first polls closed in Kentucky and Indiana at 6 PM ET (AP, 6:10 PM ET). The AP Voter Poll finds cost of living and government corruption are voters' top issues and that voters are deeply unhappy with Trump (AP, 5:13 PM ET). Democrats are favored to take the House, while they need a net gain of four seats for the Senate (Reuters, 10:35 AM ET).

  • Spain's transport minister resigned after last week's train crash that killed 69 (AFP, 6:30 PM ET).
  • King Charles called the transatlantic slave trade "a monstrous injustice" as a Commonwealth summit opened (AFP, 5:45 PM ET).
  • Paraguay's central bank chief resigned as a digital-lender crisis deepens (Reuters, 5:30 PM ET).
  • The Czech army is failing to meet NATO commitments (Reuters, 6:40 PM ET).
  • The Vatican says Pope Leo is healthy for his South America trip (Reuters, 6:20 PM ET).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 2, PM
item.description:
Iran and the Gulf

Explosions reported on Qeshm Island (unconfirmed details). Iranian state media reported at least five heavy blasts on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, along with claims that Iranian air defenses shot down a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone and captured two smaller reconnaissance drones. The cause of the blasts, the drone claims, and online reports of unannounced U.S. operations against Iranian air defenses have not been independently confirmed. Tehran also warned it would hit U.S. bases in Europe if President Trump orders strikes. (X story summary, updated about 7:05 PM ET)

Talks: no breakthrough, but contacts continue. Iran said contacts over ending the war are continuing after the latest round of talks ended without a breakthrough (Reuters, 8:50 AM ET). Earlier, Iran warned that any renewed war with the U.S. could last longer than the previous round, after Trump said he still had more targets to "take care" of (AFP, 7:08 AM ET).

Pezeshkian says the Supreme Leader granted negotiating powers. President Masoud Pezeshkian said on state media that Supreme Leader has given the government certain powers for talks and stressed dialogue over war. Oil dropped sharply on the news, with WTI briefly falling below $100 (X story summary). Reuters reported oil sliding on U.S.–Iran deal hopes as London's FTSE 100 rose for a fourth straight day (Reuters, 4:40 PM ET).

Gulf states on edge. Reuters reports Trump's Iran threat has renewed Gulf fears of "a war it didn't choose" (Reuters, 4:35 PM ET). Gulf Arab states have reportedly warned Iran they would retaliate if it attacks their infrastructure in response to any U.S. strike, and the UAE and Qatar have run security drills (X story summary). ADNOC's CEO said nearly one billion barrels have been drained from global inventories since the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted (Reuters, 11:50 AM ET).

Israel. Former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen said he believes an eventual "targeted operation" against Iran is inevitable (Times of Israel, 11:28 AM ET). Separately, Tucker Carlson claimed the U.S. could use a nuclear weapon on Iran's underground "Pickaxe Mountain" site; this is unconfirmed and not backed by officials (X story summary).

Diplomacy elsewhere. Oman's Sultan Haitham made the first Omani state visit to China in 48 years; a joint statement urged safe navigation in Hormuz and U.S.–Iran dialogue (X story summary). Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Turkmenistan (X story summary), and exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi begins a Belgium–Germany trip Tuesday ahead of accepting a freedom prize on Nov. 7 (X story summary).

Russia–Ukraine

Deadly strike on an aid point in Zaporizhzhia. Russian bombs hit a school used as a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha village. The toll has climbed through the day: AP cited Zelensky saying 18 dead (AP, 12:48 PM ET), then Reuters reported 24 (Reuters, 1:40 PM ET) and later 26, citing emergency services (Reuters, 5:45 PM ET). Zelensky called it a deliberate double-tap strike that killed rescuers and police; Russia has not commented.

New peace talks set. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff announced U.S.–Russia–Ukraine trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11 (Kyiv Independent, 6:54 PM ET). U.S. negotiators also meet European allies, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week on security guarantees (X story summary). EU officials told the Kyiv Independent the bloc is unlikely to accept a U.S. proposal to resume Russian gas flows to Europe through Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 10:08 AM ET).

Zelensky's Patriot offer. In a Fox News interview, Zelensky offered a one-month pause in strikes on Russian refineries in exchange for a month's supply of Patriot missiles, which Ukraine would pay for (X story summary).

Alert-app hacks. Both Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps were hacked overnight, sending false warnings of air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks (Reuters, 11:55 AM ET). Zelensky later confirmed Ukraine targeted Russian alert systems in retaliation (Kyiv Independent, 6:08 PM ET).

Oleshky truce fallout. Ukraine says Russia used the six-day Oleshky humanitarian truce to rearm, while Moscow assumes Kyiv did the same (Reuters, 8:45 AM ET). The Kremlin ruled out more operations like it for now (Kyiv Independent, 12:02 PM ET).

  • Russian attacks killed 2 and injured over 30 in the past day, with power outages in 10 regions (Kyiv Independent, 10:43 AM ET).
  • Ukraine's General Staff claims a record 2,500 Russian personnel losses on Nov. 1; this is Ukraine's own figure (Kyiv Independent, 7:29 AM ET).
  • Ukrainian intelligence (HUR) says a Su-57 was destroyed in an engine fire at Akhtubinsk airfield (Kyiv Independent, 8:23 AM ET), and that Russia has adapted its Gerbera decoy drone for one-way attacks up to 1,200 km (Kyiv Independent, 11:30 AM ET).
  • Russian media outlet Verstka reports the Defense Ministry will delay troop salary payments, except for forces fighting in Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 12:05 PM ET).
  • Russia formally left the Council of Europe's anti-torture convention (Kyiv Independent, 7:33 AM ET).

Other Conflicts

Gaza. Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, medics said (Reuters, 7:40 AM ET).

Colombia. A truck bomb near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, killed four people, including a two-month-old baby, and injured at least 15. Local reports blame FARC dissidents; that attribution is not yet confirmed (X story summary).

Top World News

Ebola in DR Congo. The Bundibugyo-strain outbreak has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths across eight provinces, making it Congo's deadliest Ebola epidemic; cases have been reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria, and Africa CDC is urging all countries to step up surveillance (X story summary).

Press freedom. On the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, UN Secretary-General Guterres warned of rising impunity, and UNESCO reported an 86% impunity rate for journalist killings (X story summary).

item.description:
Covering roughly 7 PM Sunday to 7 AM Monday ET. Items marked "unconfirmed" come from claims or X story summaries that haven't been independently verified.

Iran and Israel–Iran

Talks in Doha, threats on both sides. Oil fell more than 3% Monday morning, with Brent dipping below $114 a barrel, on reports of indirect US–Iran talks in Doha. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran won't move its 60% enriched uranium stockpile and wants the US naval blockade ended and sanctions relief before any deal; officials describe a draft proposal circulating and possible follow-up talks (X news summary).

At a rally in Dubuque, Iowa, Sunday night, President Trump said the US has already damaged Iran's capabilities and that the conflict would end "very soon, one way or another." Iran warned that any renewed war could last longer than the previous round, after Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets (AFP). Unconfirmed: reports circulating on X describe discussions of post-election strikes and timing talks with Netanyahu (X news summary).

Gulf on edge. Gulf diplomats, per Bloomberg and Financial Times reporting summarized on X, fear fresh US–Israeli strikes on a better-prepared Iran could bring heavier retaliation against energy sites and Hormuz shipping (X news summary).

Tankers hit. UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles about 72 nautical miles east of Ras al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia, on Nov. 1, crew safe; a separate Mayday came from the Strait of Hormuz after another vessel was hit. Iran's IRGC Navy claimed the ships hit its naval mines on an "unauthorized route" (X news summary). Qatar also condemned an attack Friday on its LNG carrier Al Mayeda in the Gulf; all 25 crew were unharmed (X news summary).

Diplomacy. China's Wang Yi met Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing Monday and urged dialogue; Beijing plans a special envoy trip to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month (X news summary). FM Abbas Araghchi is in Turkmenistan for a one-day visit on trade and energy (X news summary). Reza Pahlavi begins a Belgium–Germany trip Nov. 3 and will accept the Friedrich Naumann Foundation's Freedom Prize in Frankfurt on Nov. 7 (X news summary).

Israel

Post-election coalition maneuvering continues. The Times of Israel reports the anti-Netanyahu bloc won a combined 67 seats but faces a hard path to forming a government (Times of Israel). Avigdor Liberman says he'll recommend Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister and Yair Lapid for Knesset speaker (Times of Israel).

In Gaza, Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians Monday, per Gaza health officials, after eight were reported killed Sunday; Israel says it targeted militants and accuses Hamas of ceasefire violations (X news summary). Israeli forces pulled back from key Hebron neighborhoods after an 11-day operation that displaced more than 3,300 Palestinians (X news summary).

Russia–Ukraine

Massive drone barrage. Russia ended a roughly 48-hour assault late Nov. 1 that reportedly involved more than 1,400 drones aimed at substations, rail lines and airbases in 22 of 24 regions, causing blackouts in cities including Kyiv and Dnipro (X news summary; drone total unconfirmed). A Russian drone strike near a vocational school dormitory in Vinnytsia Oblast on Nov. 1 killed a 13-year-old girl and a woman and injured several children (X news summary).

Zelensky's offers. Zelensky says he's ready to meet Putin in Turkey, calling Ankara a realistic mediator (Kyiv Independent). In a Fox News interview he proposed pausing strikes on Russian refineries for a month in exchange for US Patriot missiles over that period (X news summary).

Losses and the front. Ukraine's General Staff claims a record 2,500 Russian casualties on Nov. 1 and 54,400 in October (Ukrainian figures, not independently verified). Not yet confirmed by a major wire in this window.

Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents. An X story summary reports the IRGC claimed four tankers hit naval mines on "unauthorized routes," plus separate reports of a projectile strike on the Qatari-owned LNG tanker Al Mayeda and limpet mines on the Panama-flagged Louise 1. Oman evacuated 25 crew from a burning tanker; no deaths were reported, and US Central Command said main shipping lanes remain clear (X story, updated 5:20 PM Sat). Details remain unconfirmed.

Record Russian losses. Ukraine's General Staff says Russia lost an estimated 54,400 troops killed or wounded in October, its worst month of the full-scale war (Kyiv Independent, 5:01 AM). These are Ukrainian figures and can't be independently verified.

Ukrainian drones hit Lukoil's Kstovo (NORSI) refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, reportedly the third strike in three days; the regional governor said over 100 drones were downed (X story, 5:16 AM). Damage extent is unconfirmed. Ukraine restarted refinery strikes Oct 30 after a two-week pause (X story).

Energy war. Russian missile and drone attacks on Oct 30 cut power to about 200,000 households in Dnipro and over 80,000 in Kyiv; Ukraine said it struck a solid rocket fuel plant in Russia's Rostov region (X story).

Diplomacy. ISW assesses the Kremlin is refusing to budge from its 2022 maximalist demands while ignoring Zelensky's offers of large-scale frontline ceasefires (ISW, 8:16 PM Sat). Lavrov said Zelensky is welcome in Moscow with security guarantees; Kyiv remains skeptical, and US-involved talks may resume in Abu Dhabi (X story).   • Sudan: Sudan filed a UN Security Council complaint accusing Ethiopia of allowing drones to launch from its territory; a Darfur market strike killed at least 102 people, and the UN Secretary-General condemned the attacks (X story).
  • India: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in Manipur state (Reuters, 4:45 AM).

Top World News

  • Germany: Masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt Saturday as large demonstrations turned violent; police used water cannon against youths throwing Molotov cocktails (AFP, 5:04 AM). Interior Minister Dobrindt called for tough penalties (Reuters, 6:40 AM).
  • Binance: The exchange resumed bitcoin and ether withdrawals after covering most of the roughly $6.3 billion stolen in a hack the FBI attributed to North Korea (AFP, 4:02 AM; Reuters, 6:10 AM).

  • Bolivia declared a state of emergency over El Niño impacts (AFP, 4:30 AM).
  • Malaysia Airlines says customers may be affected by the Amadeus data breach (Reuters, 3:00 AM).
